This chill late-night hangout in the West has everything in one spot. Private karaoke rooms for different group sizes, darts, pool, a live band, & a solid range of food & drinks (from burgers, seafood, pastas & truffle fries to steaks and even pork innards) — they’ve got you covered for a fun night out with friends.

We had their Crisp-battered Dory Fish and Chips ($18.80) which had generous fish meat that was soft and melt-in-the-mouth, paired with a crispy batter. Our fav dish, hands down!

Chargrilled Pork Collar w Baby Spuds ($24.80) was decent — a classic pork collar dish with a good portion size.

I’m not really an innards person, but bf said their Small Intestines ($12.80) was decent & well-braised! We paired it with sambal belachan, which we appreciated for its spicy punch.

Signature Thai Fish Cake ($12.80) was nicely seasoned with an ideal bouncy texture.

Golden Crispy Hashbrown ($12.80) is a simple classic side that was nicely crisp !!

Was quite disappointed with their Margarita ($18) actually… alcohol potency was alright, but the general consensus was that the drink had a slightly musty smell :”)

Flaming Lamborghini ($48) was honestly a pretty cool experience !! The flaming pour makes it feel like a mini show at your table. It leans on the sweeter side — creamy and dangerously smooth thanks to the coffee liqueur, though at $48, it does feel like you’re mostly paying for the theatrics.

We opted for their white chrysanthemum + rose + jasmine + lily Floral Tea ($12) blend, though personally I felt the tea notes could be a little stronger!

PS: you can catch their live band every Mon-Sat from 8pm-12am !!

They also offer FREE 3h KTV session from 3pm-1230am, with minimum $88 spend on drinks/alcohol & is valid Mon-Thurs only (not valid on Fri-Sun, PH & PH eves).

Located within the prestigious Orchid Country Club, 8 Degree Lounge offers an exceptional blend of comfort, style, and entertainment. Whether you're a member of the country club or a casual guest looking for a laid-back yet sophisticated night out, this lounge delivers an experience that is both memorable and refreshingly different.

The first thing that stands out about 8 Degree Lounge is its chic and contemporary design. The ambiance is modern yet cozy, with dim lighting, plush seating, and a thoughtfully arranged layout that allows for both intimate conversations and social gatherings. The atmosphere strikes a perfect balance—casual enough to feel relaxed, yet upscale enough to make the evening feel special.

What truly elevates the experience at 8 Degree Lounge is the impeccable service. From the moment you walk in, the staff greets you with warm smiles and genuine hospitality. The servers are attentive without being intrusive, and the bartenders are skilled, friendly, and passionate about their craft. Whether you’re ordering a classic whiskey on the rocks or a unique signature cocktail, you can expect precision, quality, and presentation that impress.

Speaking of drinks, the lounge offers an extensive and well-curated selection of beverages. The cocktail menu is creative, featuring a mix of timeless favorites and innovative house specials. Wine lovers will appreciate the thoughtful variety of reds, whites, and sparkling options, while beer drinkers can choose from both local and international labels. Their premium whiskey and spirits collection also adds a luxurious touch for those who enjoy the finer things.

In addition to drinks, 8 Degree Lounge offers a delectable selection of bar bites and sharing platters. The food menu complements the drinks perfectly, with offerings like crispy calamari, truffle fries, grilled skewers, and cheese boards—all expertly prepared and ideal for a relaxed dining experience. Each dish is served fresh and flavorful, enhancing the overall satisfaction of your visit.

Entertainment is another major highlight. The lounge frequently features live music performances and DJs, creating a vibrant energy without being overwhelming. The acoustics are well-managed, allowing guests to enjoy the music while still being able to hold conversations comfortably. Theme nights and special events keep the experience fresh and exciting for regular visitors.

Another plus is the setting within Orchid Country Club, which means guests also enjoy the beautiful surrounding views and the sense of exclusivity that comes with the location. Whether you're winding down after a game of golf or simply stopping in for an evening drink, the backdrop enhances the overall mood and elevates the experience.

In conclusion, 8 Degree Lounge at Orchid Country Club is a hidden gem for those seeking a refined yet approachable lounge experience. With its stylish ambiance, outstanding service, top-tier drinks, delicious food, and excellent entertainment, it has all the ingredients of a great night out. Whether for a quiet date night, after-work drinks, or a lively gathering with friends, 8 Degree Lounge consistently delivers on quality and atmosphere.

This is a good meepok fishball noodle. You will love the fishcake. I would say that they have a chance to be GREAT, with just 1 change.
The noodle is relatively taut, I wish it could be tauter--so that it has a nice bite. No, it's not soft and lumpy, no, it still has a nice bite.
The soup is great, it has a hint of Tang Chye (Preserved salted vegetable). IMHO, I think this is the key flavoring ingredient, started from the very beginning--50 years ago, eversince I was a kid.
I love the fishcake, it is firm with a nice tautness in the mouth, and a very normal fish flavour. Some fishcakes are... smell-less, yeah it sounds weird, but it is true, because it has not enough fish in it? Too much flour?
The chilli paste to noodle ratio is perfect. It has a nice flavourful mix where every bite is so satisfying. I would say it leans to the sweet side, because it lacks vinegar.
The biggest weakness is the fishball; it is too soft, it feels like it is made largely of flour, not enough firm fish meat. I think these fishballs are factory made, not handmade by them. When you bite into it, it feels light and soft. So this costs them 1 Star in this review.
I would go back to eat, if I happen to be in Novena. If you are there, please check them out. Add additional fish cake to your meepok.

If ever I make another Journey to the West, I might actually pop by again to try out more stuff from this stall.

The menu is simple yet satisfying, catering to both adults and children with familiar flavors.

One of the highlights of Ah Meng Restaurant is its family-friendly atmosphere. The seating area is spacious, clean, and comfortable, with indoor and outdoor options available. The casual setup makes it easy to relax and enjoy a break between exploring the zoo.

The staff are generally friendly and helpful, managing orders efficiently even during peak hours. Food is served promptly, which is great for visitors with children or limited time in the park. While prices are slightly higher than outside options, the convenience of being inside the zoo makes it worthwhile.

Overall, Ah Meng Restaurant is a reliable and convenient dining spot during a Singapore Zoo visit. It provides decent food, friendly service, and a comfortable environment, making it an ideal place to refuel before continuing the wildlife adventure.

Came here for Chinese New Year Eve dinner expecting a proper reunion-style experience. The atmosphere for CNY was there but the execution fell short.

Food quality was so-so. Nothing terrible, nothing memorable. For a CNY set dinner at this price point, the dishes felt rushed and lacked refinement.

Dinner started at 8:15pm, but it felt like we were being pushed to finish by 10pm. Dishes came out extremely fast, one after another, which killed the pacing of the meal. It felt more like a turnover operation than a festive dinner meant to be enjoyed slowly with family.

CNY atmosphere was present. There was Chinese opera, face-changing performance, and live singing between courses. However, the volume was excessively loud. Conversation at the table was almost impossible unless you were shouting. The only voice clearly audible was the MC on the microphone.

Overall experience was not good. For Chinese New Year Eve, people come for warmth, flow, and time together. This felt rushed, noisy, and transactional. Not an experience I would repeat for CNY.

Compliment for Excellent Service at Basilico
I would like to take a moment to share my sincere appreciation for the wonderful dining experience my associate and I had at Basilico last evening at 7:00 pm.

Upon arrival, we were warmly welcomed by Moo, who thoughtfully escorted us to a quiet corner after understanding that we were there for a business meeting. Her attentiveness immediately set the tone for a pleasant evening.

Shortly after we were seated, Restaurant Managers Melody and Fareez personally came by to greet us, which we found to be a very thoughtful gesture. Their presence reflected strong leadership and genuine hospitality.

We were then served by Eva, who was extremely professional, knowledgeable, and attentive throughout the evening. She made us feel very comfortable and confidently recommended several signature dishes from the menu. We happily followed her suggestions, and they did not disappoint.

The cold platter, carbonara, and lamb chop were all excellent—deliciously prepared and cooked to our preferred doneness by Chef Davide and his team. Every dish was outstanding.

Overall, we truly enjoyed the hospitality and service provided. It was a wonderful evening, and the team made our business meeting both comfortable and memorable.

Please convey my compliments to Manager Melody and Fareez for their impeccable leadership in guiding such a great team. Special thanks also to Eva, who ensured throughout the evening that all our dining needs were well taken care of, serving us with grace, professionalism, and deep knowledge of the menu.

Basilico is certainly a place I would highly recommend for any occasion. Thank you to the entire team for such a great experience.

The staff were also very friendly and attentive, which made the whole dining experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, it’s a great place for a family meal. We truly enjoyed our dinner and will definitely be back again!

Restaurant is a nostalgic rustic beauty so different from mall chains and over-priced eateries with some view. This place gives you the entire Sembawang Park, beach and clear view of Johor!
We felt so well taken care of by the very warm, welcoming and helpful wait team and manager Daniel who made our lunch so memorable.
Chicken satay was tender and bite-sized. Soft soy steamed halibut with tofu is easy on the tummy too and the sweet pumpkin slices in the cereal prawns made the dish less sinful. Thank you for a lovely meal!

Rustic charm and easy vibe. Not to mention, hearty unpretentious food. On a personal note, this place has beautiful memories for my wife and her family here. Celebrating her 20th and 40th birthdays here and recreating the same pose was magic.

Stopped by Bee Chiang Hiang at 702 Ang Mo Kio Ave 8 and spotted a great promo — buy 2 boxes of Golden Floss Rolls or Crispy Chicken Rolls for the price of one! Naturally, we had to try both. 😋✨

Golden Floss Rolls – A crunchy, irresistible snack filled with savoury pork floss that you just can’t put down. Perfect for a nibble anytime!

A perfect snack to munch on or share with friends!

Most places Aglio Olio is spicy, but theirs isn't, but fair enough, still doesn't taste that good. Overall, my impression is, the chef is just trained to cook but doesn't know how to taste or what is good tasting. The herbal and tom yum boat noodles were both on point, super flavourful, and perfectly balanced. The price is honestly crazy — only $0.80 per bowl! We ordered quite a lot and our total came up to just $12.50. Couldn’t even believe our eyes when the bill came. Considering how tasty everything was, this easily became one of my favourite supper spots in SG.

Another bonus: the place closes at 2am, so it’s perfect if you’re out late and craving something comforting and affordable. The vibe is casual, quick, and perfect for a late-night bite with friends.

Honestly, if you’re missing ORTO’s boat noodles or just want cheap, shiok noodles late at night, this spot is a must-try. Full marks for flavour, price, and convenience.

这次我们尝了干捞和汤的虾面。干捞版本拌上辣椒、油葱和酱汁后，味道更直接，香气也更突出；汤的版本则带有虾壳熬出来的鲜甜，喝起来顺口，不会过于厚重。虾只新鲜，口感结实，整体是一碗吃得舒服又踏实的虾面。配上的五香小吃也不错，蘸着辣椒酱吃，很有传统南洋小吃的感觉。

整体来说，这里吸引我的，不是精致的包装，而是一份朴实却舒服的用餐体验。虾面味道踏实，小吃也有传统风味，是一家会让人想轻轻松松坐下来吃一餐的店。

Seems like a family owned establishment, the soup is hearty and ingredients are generous. It’s $7 for the smallest bowl but it’s enough. The flavours packed broth was balanced  ( you can taste the herbs, pepper, and sweetness of pork rib in it). Invariably this will be a comforting dish in cool rainy day.

The food, not terrible, not offensive, but certainly not the heroic Mediterranean triumph one might expect given the rather formidable bill that awaited us at the end.

The seafood platter, while promising in theory, appeared to have endured a slightly overzealous relationship with heat. The fish arrived rather dry, and the shrimp clung on it’s shell with dear life, though in places surrendering into a puzzling mushiness that gave the faint impression of having recently completed a long residency in the freezer.

The lamb shanks were perfectly adequate, though they possessed the culinary charisma of a polite handshake.

And yet, redemption appeared in the form of the dips. We ordered four, and every single one was delightful. Paired with warm pita bread that arrived soft and generously portioned, this humble lineup became the undisputed star of the table.

The baklava diverged somewhat from the versions we’ve encountered elsewhere but remained pleasant enough. The kunafa arrived perfuming the table with glorious buttery aromas, only to deliver a surprisingly restrained flavour profile, the cheese light, delicate, and perhaps just a touch shy of making a proper statement.

Our final bill, which admittedly reflects the enthusiastic ordering habits of 2 people who perhaps momentarily forgot they were only 2 people, landed somewhere around the $400 mark. While the food was decent, we don’t believe it quite justified such a robust price tag.

Still, the staff were so lovely that the birthday lunch remained an enjoyable affair regardless.

Nestled in the historic Seletar Airport precinct, Botanico at The Summerhouse provides an idyllic escape from the city's hustle and bustle. The grill, powered by Wood Charcoal, Binchōtan, and Apple Wood, is the star of the show, adding a nuanced smoky flavor to every dish while preserving the ingredients' natural essence and nutritional integrity.

The menu showcases commitment to sustainability, with over 20 varieties of herbs and vegetables featured on the menu are grown onsite in the restaurant’s edible garden.

Some highlights include:
🌟Foie Gras Kaya Toast ($12++)
An imaginative twist on the classic Singaporean breakfast, featuring house-made foie gras kaya on chargrilled brioche, perfectly balancing sweet and savory notes.

🍔Wagyu Bun ($45++)
High-quality sliced and chargrilled Japanese Wagyu with bulgogi sauce, perilla leaves, onions, and pickled daikon, all wrapped in fluffy lotus leaf buns.

🐟Sichuan Boiled Fish ($65++)
Inspired by Chengdu Grilled Fish, this dish features a whole seasonal fish with farm-grown vegetables, bathed in a tantalizing mala sauce with Schezuan peppercorns, perfect for sharing with a side of Butterfly Blue Pea Pandan Rice ($6++).

🦆Wood-Fired Grilled Duck ($34++)
Served with baby leeks and a subtle angelica sauce made from locally-sourced traditional Chinese angelica root.

🌟Min Jiang Kueh ($18++)
A playful homage to the fluffy, nostalgic peanut pancake, featuring rich peanut ice cream and crispy peanut tuile on a light, airy corn-flavored sponge.

🍸Botanico’s garden cocktails, featuring freshly harvested herbs, perfectly complement the menu. Enjoy refreshing drinks like the Botanico Sling ($18++) and the Choco Sesame Old Fashioned ($18++), which adds a playful Asian twist with bourbon, chocolate bitters and sesame oil.

Reviews:
Canadian Pizza at Limbang never fails to impress — whether I’m dining in, picking up, or getting it delivered.

Dine-in: The place is cozy, clean, and the staff are always welcoming. Service is fast, and the pizzas come out hot and fresh. The crust is crispy, toppings are generous, and the flavors are consistently good — my personal favorite is the Singapura Special.

Takeaway: Easy and convenient. My orders are always ready on time, neatly packed, and still warm by the time I get home. No missing items, and quality is just as good as dining in.

Delivery: Super reliable. They’re usually early or right on time, and the pizzas arrive hot, not soggy like some other places. The drivers are polite, and the food is packed well to avoid any mess. Even during peak hours, they handle orders smoothly.

I also love their 2-for-1 deals — great value for money. Whether it’s a quick lunch, family dinner, or a weekend treat, Canadian Pizza CCK is one of the best.

Highly recommended!

Incredible Experience at Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza! 🍕SG

I honestly cannot recommend Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza enough! From start to finish, my experience with them was nothing short of fantastic, and I feel like every detail deserves praise. First off, the delivery was unbelievably fast! 🚗💨 I placed my order and, in no time at all, the pizzas arrived at my doorstep hot, fresh, and ready to enjoy. In this day and age, it’s rare to find a place that prioritises speed without compromising quality, and Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza nailed it perfectly.

The pizzas themselves were absolutely delicious and packed with generous toppings. 🍕😋 I ordered a couple, and every slice was loaded with cheese, meats, and veggies. You can really taste the care and quality in every bite — none of that stingy topping nonsense you sometimes get elsewhere. The crust was cooked just right: crispy on the edges, soft in the middle, and perfect for holding all the toppings together.

Another thing I loved was how affordable the pizzas were. 💰 Compared to other pizza chains, the prices are super reasonable, yet the quality is top-notch. It’s rare to find a place that combines tasty, generous pizzas with great value, and Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza delivered on both fronts.

To top it all off, they even included a free fridge magnet with my order! 🧲 I know it’s a small gesture, but honestly, it made the experience even more memorable and enjoyable. It’s clear that they put thought into making customers feel appreciated, and it really shows that they care about providing not just food, but a full, positive experience.

The staff behind the scenes must be doing something right, because everything was smooth, friendly, and efficient. From ordering to delivery, it felt like a seamless process, and I could tell they take pride in their service. 🙌

Overall, I am beyond impressed with Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza. Fast delivery, affordable prices, generous and delicious toppings, and even a thoughtful little freebie — what more could you ask for? 🍕💯 I’ll definitely be ordering from them again, and I highly recommend them to anyone who loves great pizza, excellent service, and awesome value. This is easily one of the best pizza experiences I’ve had in a long time, and it deserves every bit of a 5-star rating!

This was our third time staying at Capella Singapore. Every time it evokes the same feeling that our stay was always too short. From the moment we checked in, Hui Yi, the front office manager ensured a seamless check in process. She even followed up efficiently to ensure all the necessary admin matters was resolved efficiently (as we redeemed our GHA Discovery points to pay for our stay). Our stay was pretty routine, daily breakfast at Fiamma, lounge around the resort, afternoon tea at the Living Room (satisfactory selection of canapés and snacks), evening swim at the pool (amidst the lush greenery),  sunset dinner at Bob’s Bar. Eat, swim, sleep, and repeat. Perfect holiday for our family. Our whims and fancies were perfectly entertained by Yuki, who was more than helpful in ensuring our stay was nothing short of prefect. The most important aspect that Capella Singapore is great at, is attending to all our needs, so we can spend our precious family time just relaxing and spending time with each other. Daily breakfast at Fiamma is hands down the best breakfast at any hotel we’ve stayed in (in terms of the ala carte and buffet selection). When it gets busy (usually between 930am - 1015am), it may be a bit of a challenge to get a staff’s attention, but when you do, service is great. The duty manager (an Indian gentleman whom I forgot the name) is always on hand to make sure you get what you need, and always with a smile. It was great meeting him again, and look forward to seeing him again during our next stay (that’s right, we are already planning our next stay). In summary, each stay at Capella is always more memorable than the last, and we always look forward to our next stay at Capella Singapore. Thank you to everyone at Capella Singapore for taking such great care of us when we stay at your property. True hospitality at its finest.

Having read countless 5-star reviews about Capella, I was excited to finally experience what many call an “unofficial 6-star” hotel for a special occasion that is worth a splurge. Unfortunately, my stay did not quite live up to the hype.

For a room priced at nearly SGD 2,000 per night, I expected a much more exceptional experience.

The villa itself was undeniably spacious, but it lacked any meaningful view, which made it feel somewhat underwhelming. For a property of this calibre, I was also surprised by the bathroom facilities — the WC was a conventional type with a cold seat and no bidet spray, which felt like a basic omission at this price point, especially when smart toilets are commonly seen in most hotels these days.

The private pool was another letdown. It wasn’t large enough for a proper swim, yet not designed like a jacuzzi either — essentially just a dipping pool. We had initially planned to use it, but the presence of insects and leaves in the water made it unappealing.

Breakfast was decent, with a reasonable menu selection, but the buffet spread itself lacked variety and didn’t stand out compared to other luxury hotels.

I also tried the Auriga Spa. While the massage was satisfactory, it didn’t justify the high price. The spa facilities were particularly disappointing — no sauna, and only limited amenities such as a steam room, hot pool, and mist rooms. Many hotels in Singapore at a much lower price point offer far more comprehensive spa experiences.

On a positive note, I really appreciated the direct access to Palawan Beach, the pet-friendliness and both the Italian and Chinese restaurants were excellent.

Overall, while there were some enjoyable aspects, I found it difficult to justify the nightly rate. I had hoped for a more memorable and luxurious experience, but unfortunately, this visit fell short of expectations.

Every dish was well executed — the beef was flavourful and tender, the marinated chicken was juicy, and the kimchi pancake with prawns was satisfying with a nice balance of crispness and flavour. The ginseng chicken soup was comforting and hearty.

What truly stood out was the service. The waitress wearing spectacles was extremely patient, polite, and genuinely cheerful throughout. She cooked both the beef and chicken for us over charcoal and thoughtfully removed the charcoal once everything was done so we wouldn’t feel the heat — a very considerate touch that made the experience even more comfortable.

The total bill came to about $245 including GST for the both of us, and honestly it felt well worth it given the quality of food and attentive service. Parking was also incredibly convenient, literally right at the doorstep, which made the visit very hassle-free.

Overall, a very enjoyable experience and we would happily return.

Had such a satisfying meal at Daily Chef Wen! 🍽️ Everything we ordered was packed with flavor and beautifully prepared.

The Beef Sourdough with Grilled Caramelized Onion was another standout—crispy sourdough topped with flavorful beef and sweet caramelized onions made it really satisfying.

Had lunch on a quiet Sunday at Chilli Padi Tok Panjang — the space is large, peaceful, and almost empty at midday, making it an easy, comfortable choice for families and groups. The buffet is good value for money, with a decent spread and well-prepared dishes.

Chilli Padi Tok Panjang celebrates Peranakan heritage through the traditional tok panjang feast — the iconic long-table communal dining experience. The buffet highlights classics like Ayam Buah Keluak, Babi Pongteh, Chap Chye, and Sambal Udang, all prepared with time-honoured rempahs and traditional methods that bring out the depth and richness of true Nyonya flavours.

A calm, family-friendly spot with hearty Peranakan staples and plenty of room to dine unhurried — a lovely choice for a relaxed weekend meal.

​A fantastic lunch outing today at the renowned Chinatown Complex Hawker Centre. My picks were the 烧鸭+烧肉饭 (Roast Duck + Roast Pork Rice) at Old Master Hong Kong Charcoal Grill, and the comforting 苦瓜排骨汤 (Bitter Gourd Pork Rib Soup) from 宝中宝.

Locally, this is arguably one of the best food complexes, as you've noted, the food choices are incredibly varied and delicious. It truly offers an abundance of good options for a meal.

Chinatown Complex Food Court is a vibrant hub that captures the essence of Singapore’s hawker culture. Nestled in the heart of Chinatown, it boasts one of the largest collections of food stalls under one roof, offering everything from traditional dim sum and claypot rice to Michelin-recognized hawker gems. The atmosphere is bustling yet welcoming, with locals and tourists mingling over affordable, authentic dishes. Beyond the food, the space reflects the cultural richness of the area, with its lively chatter and communal dining style. It’s not just a place to eat—it’s an experience that celebrates heritage, flavor, and community in every bite.

I had the Hokkien mee for lunch and it was really good—flavourful, well-balanced, and satisfying. The price starts from a minimum of $6, which feels reasonable for the portion and quality. The only downside was the environment—the food centre was quite warm and humid during lunchtime, which made the experience a bit uncomfortable. I think it would be a much more pleasant visit in the evening when it’s cooler. Overall, still worth trying for the tasty Hokkien mee!

(Ate in January 2026) We were at Bangkit market to buy some durians during durian season, and walked past this store. The store uncle said that they had a new dry noodle dish and asked us to try it. I asked if it was like chilli ban mian, or the regular dry ban mian, he said no and added that it was unlike anything found elsewhere. Since I was a huge fan of dry noodles in general, I decided to give it a try.

It was indeed very delicious. As there was some vinegar added, it seemed like a mix between ban mian and bar chor mee. The mouthfeel of the noodles was very satisfying given that they were handmade, and the sauce was also well balanced. While it was slightly more expensive, there were many ingredients. Only one criticism I have was that there was not enough noodles, and I got myself another bowl!

I hope they keep this dish on the permanent menu.

Reviews:
Coastes has been our favourite for years and continues to be the best cafe in sentosa beach. Not sure what’s up with the bad reviews.
We came for brunch and the food has been consistently good for the past 5 years. The brunch prices are also reasonable for Singapore, much less Sentosa! They also have the most extensive day time offerings compared to the other beach cafes here. The staff were so kind, they shifted the umbrellas to shield us and when I said thank you, they said don’t be shy to ask help from us.
It has direct access to the beach and our kids can play with the sand in peace while parents sip on some drinks. There are often promos! We got 2 sangrias for $18. Yes the drinks are expensive $5 and up but it’s sentosa and even bubble tea is $4 nowadays. So give them a break, be kind and objective. There were people of all personalities- Singaporeans, foreigner Chinese, Caucasians etc. everyone was happy. Be chill and be merry and appreciate our long-time coastes more!

Disappointing service in Northpoint on 13 March 2026, dinner. We saw the promotion for the free pizza with Citibank card payments, and hence ordered to the subtotal of $60. My initial order was only $50.90, but we added a $10 truffle fries to be able to hit the minimum subtotal of $60.

We then proceeded to ask a blonde-bun haired lady about the promotion, to which she checked and told us we were at $58.50 subtotal, as the set wasn’t included. Hence, we ordered a $4 coke to top up to $60. We then asked a guy who was serving us food to help us order the pizza, who said he’d check but didn’t come back.

When we were half done with our food, we decided to ask another lady about the promotion, who told us she’d check and get back to us. However, she only returned after around 15 minutes (after we were almost done with our food) to tell us that we hadn’t hit the minimum order, as it was now $64.90 including the set ($58 subtotal for ala carte).

This was after being told that we were only $1.50 away, and already adding so much in order to hit the $60 minimum, on top of which we had waited so long. She then started arguing with me and insisting that we were away from the $60. I would’ve understood if she simply apologised for their mistake as it was a mislook, but insisting that I was wrong when your staff clearly said we were less than $2 away is wrong. She later offered to void the coke from the payment, which I accepted. However, she went on to tell me that there was no way the other staff would have said $58.50, as that figure didn’t show up or make sense, and told me that i had the QR code on my phone and should’ve checked too.

Honestly, it’s an internal staff issue if they are unaware of how to compute this subtotal. I had already accepted the void coke and was willing to move on from it, but she went on to tell me about how I was wrong instead of apologising, or checking with the other staff if she had made a mistake.

Throughout this, there was not a single apology accepted. This is extremely disappointing and upsetting. As a frequent visitor to the Nex outlet, this dinner has just been a big disappointment.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Garlic Naan & Mutton Keema – Simply Outstanding at Drubinah Yishun

I recently tried the garlic naan with mutton keema at Drubinah Yishun and it was nothing short of amazing. The naan arrived warm, fluffy and perfectly baked, with just the right balance of crisp edges and soft centre. The garlic flavour was fragrant but not overpowering, making every bite incredibly satisfying even on its own.

The real star, however, was the mutton keema. It was rich, well-spiced and packed with deep, authentic flavours. The minced mutton was tender and juicy, not dry at all, and the masala was beautifully balanced without being too oily. When paired with the naan, the combination was pure comfort food at its best.

Portion size was generous and definitely value for money, especially considering the quality. Service was also fast and friendly, making the overall dining experience even better.

If you are in Yishun and craving hearty North Indian flavours, do not miss out on the garlic naan and mutton keema at Drubinah. It is easily a 5-star dish and I will definitely be back for more.

Daawat Tandoori
A homey North Indian spot that keeps things simple and comforting, Daawat Tandoori leans on familiar flavors rather than flash. It’s the kind of place where the food speaks louder than the décor, and the staff run things with a straightforward, no-nonsense warmth.

Takeaways:
• Butter Chicken isn’t the city’s best, but it’s a genuinely good rendition—creamy without being heavy, curry-forward with a touch of heat to keep things interesting.
• Paneer Makhani is solid, leaning slightly sweet from the paneer itself, which melds into the sauce nicely even if it doesn’t quite steal the spotlight.
• Dal Makhani is a solid pick for a vegetarian option. It carries enough depth and gentle heat to feel comforting without becoming too heavy.
• Naans are serviceable but could benefit from more char for that smoky lift. The garlic naan does what it should, while the paneer naan is an interesting idea that never quite lets the cheese shine. The cheese naan hints at richness but stops short of delivering fully.
• The vibe is no-frills but not hole-in-the-wall—clean, humble, and warmly familiar. Staff are pragmatic, friendly, and confident in the food they serve.

The Damage (no drinks): S$ 30-40 for two

Had a really enjoyable dinner at Daruma Tavern and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The atmosphere is lively and inviting, with that bright neon frontage giving it a fun, casual vibe — perfect for group dinners or chill nights out.
We ordered their prawn noodle and a seafood platter, and both were solid. The broth for the noodles was rich, savoury, and packed with flavour — you can tell it’s been properly cooked down. Ingredients were fresh, especially the prawns and seafood, which were juicy and sweet. The chilli added a nice kick without overpowering the dish.
The seafood platter was a highlight — generous portions, well-balanced, and great for sharing. Everything came together nicely with crispy bits, eggs, and that comforting gravy tying it all up.
Also tried their pork knuckle (didn’t manage to take a photo), and it was seriously good. The skin was perfectly crispy while the meat inside stayed tender and juicy — exactly what you want from a good pork knuckle.
Service was friendly and efficient despite the crowd, and the overall experience felt smooth. Definitely a spot I’d come back to again. Highly recommended if you’re looking for hearty, satisfying food in a casual setting.

We had a truly wonderful experience at Din Tai Fung, RWS, on Sunday evening, and I felt it was important to share this.

After spending the whole day at the beach with my mother, who is on a wheelchair, and my two teenagers, we arrived tired, sandy, and very hungry, without having had dinner yet. Despite being among the later customers, we were so well taken care of, thanks to Ms. Chun Rong (Supervisor).

We initially had difficulty ordering through the online system, but she immediately stepped in and kindly took our order manually, saving us time and stress. She also helped to expedite our food, and our fried rice arrived quickly, which meant so much to us in that moment.

What truly stood out was her attentiveness throughout the entire meal. She consistently checked on us, ensured all dishes were served, refilled our tea & condiments and even thoughtfully reminded us about the last order. Despite the restaurant being busy, she made us feel genuinely cared for.

Most importantly, she treated my mother with such kindness and respect. My mother was very happy and felt truly well taken care of.

Even my daughter, who has high expectations, was so impressed that she insisted I give a 5-star review. That says a lot.

As someone who runs a business, I know how rare it is to have staff who serve with such sincerity and heart. Ms. Chun Rong, Supervisor, is truly an asset to your team.

Thank you for making our evening so memorable. We will definitely be back.

Been a while since I last ate here. Decided to try this relatively new stall in Clementi West St 2. Ordered the $3.50 portion of mee kia dry with chilli sauce. The portion is decent for this price. It came with two fishballs and one meat ball and about 10 slices of fish cake.

First of all the accompanying soup. It didn’t taste solely made with MSG and salt. Pork bones were boiled with water and it became more umami tasting as more fishballs are boiled. The noodles could have been more al dente. Glad I did not order the soup version because the noodles would have been even soggy towards the end. With this dry version, your main focus is on the chilli sauce which was good. Not a lot of heat but fragrant and very savoury. With enough vinegar, it goes well with the noodles. Owner was also very generous with the lard and oil so that helped elevate the overall taste of the noodles

The sliced fish cakes were a joy to eat. They were fried until a crispy skin on the outside was achieved and then sliced. So as you bite down, the crispy skin contrasted against the soft core of the fish cake. But the star has the be their fishballs. Bouncy, irregular shapes and tasting full of saltiness of sea fish, every bite was a pleasure, even without dipping into cut chilli/soya sauce. As for the meat ball, it was more of fish meat and pork cause it tasted as umami as the fish balls.

Very well done as far as fishball noodles go. It’s been a while I found since such tasty fishball noodles. I must come back again soon for their mee pok.

Restaurant Name: Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice & Kitchen
Reviews:
五星鸡饭其实开了很多年了，算是这一带很老的一个招牌，大概已经有三十多年历史。以前很多人都会特地来这里吃鸡饭，因为他们家的味道一直都算稳定，也算是附近比较有名的一家老店。除了白斩鸡饭、烧鸡饭之外，其实他们也有一些家常煮炒，可以点豆腐、炒青菜、炒肉，还有一些简单的汤类，所以有时候也不只是吃一盘鸡饭，而是可以当作一顿比较完整的晚餐。

我自己平时来这里，其实比较常点他们的炒鸡饭，尤其是鸡胸肉。鸡胸肉炒过之后会比较香，也比较有一点脆口的感觉，吃起来反而比一般鸡饭更有口感，也比较下饭，所以我通常都会点这个。鸡肉整体味道是不错的，不过他们的鸡皮就没有那种很香脆的感觉，比较像是带一点烤过的味道，但不是那种脆脆的皮。

饭方面可以选择西饭或者白饭，也可以单点，或者加肉、加蛋、加豆腐等等，选择其实还蛮多的。我平时也蛮喜欢点一份豆芽配西饭一起吃。不过豆芽这道菜我觉得味道就比较普通一点，没有那种很香的锅气，反而有一点点咸鱼的味道，但又没有那种很明显的咸香感。如果在味道上再调整一下，可能会更好。

整体来说，如果只是想简简单单吃一顿饭，其实还是可以的。餐厅的位置算蛮大的，室内室外都有座位。室外大概可以坐二十多个人，有两张比较大的桌子，也有一些小桌子。室内有空调，环境就是比较传统的餐厅感觉，不是那种很新潮的装潢，但也算舒适。

服务方面是比较家庭式的感觉，很多阿姨在帮忙端菜、点菜，整体态度都蛮友善的，也有一种老店比较亲切的感觉，不会太拘谨。

不过价格方面现在其实算是比较贵了。我个人觉得和十几年前相比，他们的品质其实有一点点退步，而且这些年也没有看到太多新的创意或者新的菜式。但是价格却还是一直在提高，当然这也和现在整体的通货膨胀有关系，食材成本上升，餐饮价格普遍都变贵了。

所以现在吃起来会觉得，这里已经不是那种很便宜、很随意的鸡饭店了。虽然味道还是可以，但在现在竞争这么多的情况下，如果他们未来可以在菜式或者做法上多一点创意，或者做一些新的变化，可能会更有吸引力。现在更多还是一种老店的感觉，偶尔想吃一顿熟悉的味道的时候，可以来这里坐一坐、吃一餐。

Not wanting to make things difficult, I asked if at least 1 packet could be thigh meat. She checked with the kitchen and came back with a no.

Out of curiosity, I walked over to take a look and could clearly see chicken thigh portions still available, yet they refused to serve.

I requested a refund. The refund was processed, but the last 4 digits reflected did not match the card I used. When I asked the cashier, she mentioned it was processed according to the payment system.

After all the time wasted, I even asked again if I could proceed to buy 2 packets of chicken thigh rice. The reply was immediate, no more thighs, only breast meat.

After checking Google reviews, I realised there are similar complaints about refusal to serve thighs and poor service attitude. This is not my first time at Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice, which makes this outlet’s service quality even more disappointing.

Service transparency and consistency really need improvement.

A well known name in the catering scene with a loyal following, but this visit felt uneven.

The standout was undoubtedly the crispy roast chicken. Beautifully rendered skin with a delicate crackle, giving way to tender, juicy meat beneath. Simple, well-executed, and easily the best dish of the meal. Though notably, we had to remind the staff for the all-important pepper salt.

The rest of the spread didn’t quite reach the same heights. Flavours across several dishes felt muted and under seasoned, lacking the depth and punch you’d expect from a kitchen with such history. Execution was competent, but ultimately unmemorable. The sakura prawn scallop fried rice lacked wok hei, the wasabi prawns came cloaked in a thick, tasteless crust with a bland, almost luminous green sauce drizzled on as an afterthought, and the golden dragon chicken’s panko coating distracted from the squid paste rather than enhancing it.

Service was efficient despite the bustle. White table linen and an old-school banquet setting lend a certain nostalgic charm.

Still a dependable option for group catering.

Visited Happy Thai Food last night and had a really enjoyable experience. The place has a simple and cozy atmosphere that makes it comfortable to sit down, relax, and enjoy a good meal. The food was definitely the highlight of the visit. Everything we ordered came out hot and full of flavor. You can really taste the balance that Thai cuisine is known for, a nice mix of sweet, sour, savory, and a bit of spice, especially the sauce they gave on the side! The ingredients tasted fresh, and the dishes were well prepared. It felt like the kind of food that’s made with care rather than just rushed out of the kitchen.

Portion sizes were also quite generous, which made the meal feel like good value for money. It was satisfying without being overly heavy, and sharing a few dishes with the table made the experience even better.

Overall, Happy Thai Food is a great spot if you’re craving authentic Thai flavors in a relaxed setting. With tasty food, friendly service, and a comfortable atmosphere, it’s definitely somewhere I would come back to again and recommend to friends and family.

I ordered the Fuzhou Minced Meat Noodle (Item 3a on the menu), opting for Mee Pok. At $5.50 with extra noodles, it is a reasonably priced bowl given the portion size.
​
​Flavour Profile: The stall claims to offer "古早味" (traditional taste) dating back to 1985, and it definitely lives up to that promise. The flavour foundation is solid, largely thanks to the generous use of lard, which gave the noodles a wonderful, aromatic coating.

​The Noodles: The Mee Pok came topped with a generous heap of minced meat. Texture-wise, they were a little softer than I usually prefer. The bowl was also served a bit dry initially, but a quick drizzle of the accompanying soup solved that problem immediately, hydrating the noodles nicely and helping to mix the sauce evenly.

​The Ingredients: The highlight for me was the Fuzhou fishballs. They were excellent—bouncy on the outside and juicy on the inside with that savoury meat filling. It’s rare to find them done this well.

​The Verdict:
Despite the noodles being slightly on the soft side, the flavours here are on point. It’s a satisfying bowl of traditional noodles with great lard flavour and standout fishballs. I will definitely be coming back to try the other items on their extensive menu.

"Experience the transformative power of authentic Char Kway Teow, elevated by generous portions and vibrant vegetables that perfectly balance the dish's signature richness. Third-generation chef Mr. Tan Boon Huat brings unwavering dedication to every plate. Conveniently located just a five-minute walk from Pasir Panjang MRT, this stall offers a fresh, healthier take on a beloved classic."

Heng Huat is known for serving a “healthier” version of fried kway tiao.

A standard plate costs S$8, fried with egg, bean sprouts, cai poh & blood cockles, then topped with a huge pile of boiled cai xin (Chinese mustard greens).

Personally felt the portion wasn’t very generous. Without pork lard, Chinese sausage, or fish cake, the dish also ends up being less fragrant than the usual version. The large amount of greens tasted a bit too raw or slightly odd when paired with the noodles.

Still an interesting option if you’re looking for a lighter plate of fried kway tiao 🍜

There were no snacks or drinks served to our guests upon arrival as the BQT staff were not ready. So our guest sat at empty tables, without beverages as they waited for the wedding to start. Our lunch was abit rushed through by the staff and I (bride) was shocked the main table was cleared even before I realised it. We hated the music for the food walk in, we actually had our selected music that was not played. Again, the food was great. But the courses came too fast. Reviews:
Came on a Sunday after work at exactly 2pm, just 30 minutes before their closing time, honestly felt really bad and embarrassed as I know how tough it is having a last minute customer enter right as you’re about to go for your break.

But the service was immaculate, they were still very welcoming and I ordered a Daekji Gukbap, which came out in less than 10 minutes, it was piping hot and steaming, served alongside a tray with some Banchan, and 2 jars filled with gochujang and anchovy.

Everything looked really unassuming, especially the spinach, which I really wasn’t expecting myself to eat, as every singular Korean branch I’ve been to has messed it up, turning it either too salty or salty.

But when I took a small bite of it, it was too hard to put my chopsticks down, there was so much flavour packed in that small little veggie that tingled all my tastebuds and before I knew it, I had absolutely devoured the banchan alone by itself! How incredible is that.

Moving on to the main star, which was this comforting bowl of Daekji Gukbap served in a ceramic pot, all with the steam curling into the air still. Upon, taking my first sip of the broth alone, I was punched by the umami flavours bringing me back to the hearts of Busan. I felt like a fisherman on the seaside sprinkling anchovy and coming home to drink that warm bowl of goodness after a tiring day of fishing. It was THAT good!

The flavours and service truly bought a tear to my ears, and I found myself wanting to shed a droplet after finishing my meal. 😆💕

Their entire menu pictures are uploaded here. I've been to Michelin Star vegetarian & vegan restaurants, and iVegan stand up to all of them. What I love most about their style of cooking is... the right amount of simplicity and the fusion innovation. Simplicity is that they use good fresh ingredient in their food so you actually taste the garlic, arugula, mushrooms or veggies. Example, the beansprouts with chives, is SO SIMPLE but it taste so clean, crisp  and good! Another, Kailan nice cut into cubes and stir-fried perfectly (right timing) and top with fried garlic bits, that's it! And it taste soooooo goooood! Annother one, mushroom stems nicely cooked, so that its succulent and moist--that taste like scallop with pesto drips! So simple and so goooood!
Fusion, ok, they have Sushi with Guacamole, and it taste... so well fused. They have the wok-fried Udon with capsicum and mushroom--fresh and different. Oh yeah King Mushroom with Sichuan sauce, unique and original taste.
There's so much... oh they have snack portions of the food! So they have assorted nuts, grilled potato with tofu and mushrooms--all served as food you can talk and nibble.

I’ve heard so much about Ivins Peranakan Restaurant but never got the chance to try it until this trip, thanks to my uncle who brought us here for dinner! This is his all-time favorite spot, and it totally lived up to the hype – even on a weekday, there was still a long line outside when we finished eating at 8 PM. No advance reservation? Forget about getting a table; the popularity is off the charts!

Uncle said compared to before, the portion sizes have gotten a bit bigger now, and the prices have had a small adjustment, but the value for money is still solid. Since each dish isn’t too large (especially side dishes like lady’s finger), it’s perfect for sharing with a group. We ordered six to seven dishes altogether, got to taste a little bit of everything, and left super satisfied.

I have to rave about these must-try dishes! First up is the Five-Spice Roll – crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, it’s absolutely amazing! The outer layer is golden and crunchy, making a satisfying “crunch” when you bite into it, while the meat inside is juicy and tender, not the least bit dry. Dip it in the restaurant’s chili sauce, and the spicy, savory flavor is so appetizing. Then there’s the Preserved Radish Omelette – the golden, crispy omelet wraps around the sweet, sour, and salty preserved radish, filling the air with aroma. Every bite is crunchy and delicious, I couldn’t stop eating it. The Sweet and Sour Riblets are also fantastic – coated in a sweet sauce, they’re tangy and appetizing, making them the ultimate rice companion. Also, the Lady’s Finger with Chili is cooked just right, not too mushy, with each piece coated in chili sauce that’s flavorful and perfect for pairing with rice. Just a heads up, the portion is pretty small!

For the staple, I highly recommend the Saffron Rice! It’s way more flavorful than plain white rice – its unique aroma enhances the taste of every dish, making it a perfect match for anything. The restaurant’s counter also has Peranakan pastries; make sure to order the taro-flavored one in the picture! It has a rich taro taste, just the right amount of sweetness, and a light texture. Eating it with glutinous rice brings out the authentic Peranakan flavor – it’s incredible.

To be honest, there are a couple of minor downsides. The restaurant is clearly short-staffed, so the service is a bit slow and not very attentive. If you need something like spoons or forks, you might have to get them yourself instead of waiting for the servers to bring them over – that’s definitely something they could improve on. Also, parking is a bit of a hassle; there are only parallel parking spots available, no dedicated parking lots. If you’re driving, make sure to find a spot in advance.

Had wanted to redeem the Great Eastern Achievers vouchers with my Mum and Dad, but forgot that it was the Eve of Public Holiday (Hari Raya)!

Luckily we were attended to by Krishnan, who made the decision to allow us to redeem the vouchers on an exceptional basis.

He empathised that he had been in similar situations before and did not want to see my parents disappointed. I was really touched by him.

Thanks to Krishnan's willingness to go the extra mile, we had a wonderful family lunch and he really made our day.

I surveyed the main menu, and was enticed by the delicious offerings and promos. Will certainly return to this outlet for the food, ambience and service.

Cheers 😃

Had a wonderful dining experience at Jade Restaurant at The Fullerton Hotel. The Cantonese dishes were beautifully presented and full of flavour — especially the lobster and the roasted meats. Ingredients were fresh, sauces were well balanced, and everything was cooked perfectly. Service was attentive and professional, with an elegant ambience that’s perfect for a special occasion. Highly recommended.

Dining at Jade for the Lunar New Year is a masterclass in elegance. The restaurant’s soft jade-hued decor and bird-motif wallpaper create a stunning, sophisticated backdrop that feels both historic and fresh.

The festive menu shines with impeccable seafood. The Red Grouper was a standout—perfectly steamed, incredibly fresh, and delicate in texture. Equally impressive was the Lobster, which was succulent, expertly seasoned, and served with a refined touch that let the natural sweetness of the meat take center stage.

The staff provided exceptional, friendly service that felt personal and warm, matching the high standards of the setting without being overly formal.

A beautiful, high-end destination for the Lunar New Year where the quality of the ingredients and the grace of the staff make every moment feel special.

The prawn omelette was epic! I wish they also sold a crab meat omelette! Was lucky enough to be there on the early side for dibner because the place got very crowded 15 mins later! Staff are very friendly!

Would only return for the tom yum soup which is not enough to make me return. Service was pleasant.

This makes it an excellent choice for a focused catch-up with friends or a solo meal where you actually want to hear yourself think. It’s a reliable, low-key spot that deserves a bit more foot traffic than it gets!

No complains about having leftovers for a few more meals.
The whole process of eating jokbal is rather enjoyable and not one to have if you are jn a rush - you decide what your bite would be, construct it enveloped by the lettuce or kknaepnip (favour is more refined and fragrant, almost like a mint compared to shisho) with dipping of choice, stuff in mouth, chew and savour the lovely gelatinous pork with flavour accents and textures, swallow.. drink some alcohol.. chat.. repeat. Lovely meal routine.

But if there's only two of you, I recommend ordering the mini jokbal in their set menu as a start 😆. Service staff was also attentive. Small cosy, hole in the wall kind of shop which we like.

No photos cause we got our hands dirty soon after, but there's enough photos of jokbal for your reference in this review.

Lentor Modern, B1-04
1 Lentor Central,

🟫 Location = 🟫 Take the TEL ( Thomson East Coast line) and alight at Lentor Station. ➖️ Use Exit 1.

🟤 Lentor Modern ( ▪︎a new mall that opened in Dec 2025) is connected to Lentor Station via a underground tunnel passageway.

🔵 The interior decor of Jew Kit at Lentor Modern features a blend of traditional local heritage and modern design, incorporating clean lines, warm tones, and decorative Peranakan motif black & white floor tiles.

🔵 The use of dark wooden rattan chairs and white marble table tops lends a nostalgic vibe.

🟨 Food takeaway / Dabao 打包
***********************************
🟨Traditional Roasted Pork Hokkien Mee / SGD13.80

🟨 I am not fond of Roasted Pork.✖️ So I requested for no pork and no squid in my Hokkien Mee. The kitchen was nice enough to accede to my request.

🟠 The Hokkien Mee was scrumptious. It consisted of local thick Yellow mee and Beehoon, stir-fried in a umami-filled thick gravy broth made from prawn shells, prawn heads, and pork bones.

🟠 The essential elements of this beloved local noodle dish includes crispy pork lard, fresh prawns, eggs, and a sambal that complements the mee.

🟩 Service standards = 🟢 The staff were friendly, pleasant and efficient.

Sundays regularly find me in Yishun, where I often take a late lunch.  I must admit my initial hesitation to eat at Just Greens because of their poor rating and reviews.  Then again, if we don’t try, we never know, so guess what…?

It was good!  The vegetarian operators certainly know how to make vegetables tasty.

There were enough flavour profiles and textures to choose from, ranging from the soy sauce infused crunchy black fungus and braised mushroom, through gently salted bean curd skin ‘egg’ roll and the judiciously tomato-sauce inflections in the brinjal and long bean stir-fry.  The brown rice was unsalted and unflavoured, its mildly nutty flavours coming through in grains moist and tender, almost tending to clump.

Yet, this was the perfect complement to the variety of dishes, some of which were seasoned more gently  so that the plainer vegetables could hold their own in sauces that aren’t starchy or cloying.  Except the brinjal, which had a tendency to suck up fat, the dishes didn’t show any trace of oiliness in the mouth.  Those seeking some animal protein can take solace in an egg omelette, displayed separately from the other options.  You will also find gentle amounts of dried anchovy flavouring their spinach, belacan for their vegetable curry, etc.

My $6 bought me a satisfying meal of 4 dishes on brown or white rice.  Servings were generous so that I finished the rice before the dishes.  So, while it wasn’t exactly cheap, it certainly was value for money.  Most importantly, the meal was honest and well considered, paying due respect to the various ingredients.

* The Signature Taiwan Mazesoba: This is the undisputed star of the show. Every bowl is a masterclass in texture and flavor—the chewy, perfectly al dente noodles acting as the perfect canvas for that rich, savory minced meat and the creamy richness of the egg yolk.

* Consistent Excellence: Being a "regular" is an understatement. Even after countless visits, the quality remains top-tier. Every single time I visit, I leave as a "happy camper," satisfied by the soul-warming depth of their secret sauce.

* The King’s Privilege: There is a certain magic in returning to a place where the flavors feel like home. Having worked my way through a mountain of bowls here, I can confidently say that Kaijiken offers the most addictive dry ramen experience in Singapore.

If you’re in Tanjong Pagar and haven't tried their Taiwan Mazesoba, you are truly missing out on a weekly delicacy that defines comfort food.

Restaurant Name: Kin Kao Mai Thai Restaurant Sembawang
Reviews:
We visited Kin Kao Mai Thai at  Sembawang on 14 March 2026 for a business dinner. The food and sea view were enjoyable at first, and the evening was going well until the way we were treated at the end completely ruined the experience.
At around 10:47 PM, staff informed us the restaurant was closing. We fully respected that and immediately settled the bill. However, we still had two glasses of beer unfinished, so we politely asked if we could have a few minutes to finish them.
A male staff member then approached our table and insisted that he wanted to clear the beers immediately. We politely asked for five minutes, then even reduced it to two minutes, but he responded in a very disrespectful and aggressive tone, telling us we had “one minute” to finish our drinks.
What made this situation particularly unacceptable was that other tables nearby were still drinking beer and were not being rushed at all. Even when we left at 11:07 PM, there were still tables with full glasses of beer continuing to drink without any pressure from staff.
So the obvious question is: why were we singled out and treated differently?
We had already paid our bill and were simply finishing our drinks. The way this staff member spoke to us was unprofessional, disrespectful, and completely unnecessary. It gave the impression that certain customers are treated differently from others.
For a restaurant located far from the city center and public transport, customers come here expecting hospitality and a pleasant atmosphere. Unfortunately, the attitude of this male staff member completely destroyed the mood of what was supposed to be a professional business gathering.
Hospitality is not just about food — it is about how guests are treated. What we experienced that night was the opposite.
Management should seriously review the service conduct of their staff and explain why customers are treated inconsistently.
Until that happens, we will not be returning. There are many other restaurants nearby where guests are treated with basic respect.

Reviews:

Went on 22nd Nov 2025 for anniversary dinner. My partner knew of this place from some videos online and wanted to try the grilled maguro rib and the grilled maguro collar. We had a reservation prior to coming.
While ordering, the staff patiently responded to all our queries and explained some of dishes.
We had the maguro 5-cut sashimi. The staff explained to us the order we should eat the pieces and the corresponding parts. Despite being on the pricier side, we could tell the quality of the fish was really good. The akami, the cut which is supposed to be the least fatty, left the surface of the soy sauce with a layer of fat. The wasabi provided is also from the actual wasabi plant, not from some packaged wasabi which tend to be too spicy.
We also tried the fish heart/ventricle, which is on their seasonal menu, it tastes exactly like what you would expect innards to taste like if you had tried innards from other animals such as chicken.
The maguro rib was a surprising one for me, the charred part didn't feel like fish but you could still tell it's still fish from the meat closer to the bones.
Their hot tea has free refills btw :)
This place can accommodate large groups, there was a large family dining here as well while we were here, counter seats are also available.

Kudos to the students running the place for the food and service. The place is done up well enough though some things can be refined a little.

My overall take is that they have done well but most things could use a little improvement.

1) The pasta I had was too firm. To note I love pasta al dente but this needed a bit more time.
2) The sauce tasted good but it was too dry. Just a tad more liquidy texture would elevate it.
3) The mango sticky rice didn’t really work as a reimagined version of the dish as I would have much preferred the original. Textures, taste and mashed up taken in altogether could be improved on.
4) They only had white or raw sugar and no equal or other type of non-sugar sweetener and it would be good to have that alternative for the hot tea/coffee.

Service wise it was excellent. So great job there 👏🏻

Saying all this they will be closed for reno for a year and after that not sure what the new form will be. All the best to the students there in their f&b journey 👍🏻🙂

La Braceria Pizza & Grill offers a refined take on Italian comfort, where the charcoal grill (the "braceria") takes center stage. The "Chef’s Specials" are the clear stars, featuring a succulent Wagyu Flank Steak with chimichurri ($38).
For a standout starter, the Portobello mushrooms—oven-baked and smothered in a silky parmesan cream sauce—are practically mandatory. It’s ambiance, it’s the kind of spot where a glass of red wine feels like a requirement, not an option.
Fantastic food with a cozy atmosphere and excellent service! Chef is friendly and kind!

This was my first time visit here to celebrate my friend’s birthday.

The valet service was excellent as we were assisted by a very friendly young indian parking attendant on where to park our car. He had also recommended us to must try the pizza and cheese cake. We ordered cooked ham & mushroom pizza, it was indeed very delicious and was well received by everyone. The cheesecake was nice and delicate. For the mains, l ordered lamb chop, it was tender and not dry though well done.

However, there was a point that I would like to share. As we were seated next to the door opening, the door had been opened/closed frequently which produced a little irritated sound when it repeatedly hit onto the door knob. I think by adding a small foam on the door knob can help to reduce the sound effect so that the whole dining experience can be improved.

Overall, the ambience, food and  service were great. Highly recommended!

Table for 3 for lunch during Hari Raya.

The place has a dank smell to begin, with which does not make for a pleasant dining experience. Two people actually got seated and left without ordering.

Everything was just not fresh, rancid and the flavor profiles were just off.
I gave 2 stars because the front staff were really nice and tried their best, but I don’t think they are being supported in the backend.
It was a very sad experience.

cozy vibes, authentic Italian flavours.

Here’s what we tried:

🍟 Patatine Fritte al Profumo di Tartufo
Golden, crispy truffle fries loaded with Parmesan and fragrant black truffle. Savoury, aromatic, and honestly addictive from the first bite — perfect for sharing… or not.

🍍 Hawaiana Pizza
Thin, nicely charred crust topped with Italian tomato sauce and creamy fior di latte mozzarella. The salty ham and sweet pineapple combo hits just right — classic sweet-salty vibes done perfectly.

🍝 Fettuccine alla Carbonara
Homemade fettuccine tossed in a silky, rich sauce of egg, cream, and Parmesan. Smoky bacon adds that indulgent depth, making every bite comforting and deeply satisfying.

🍮 Crème Brûlée
The perfect sweet ending. Rich custard base with a layer of caramelized sugar on top — crack through the warm sugar to the chilled, creamy custard below. Absolute dessert goals.

I was so engrossed in eating that I forgot to take photos — which probably says everything you need to know. Highly recommended if you’re craving authentic Thai food made with heart!

The authentic Thai food is top notched.  Check out the king prawns! Thank you host-cum-chef Terrence and Laddas for the warm reception and gracious hospitality.  Highly recommended!  This is a must-try!

My parents had the fisherman dish. She felt the fried fish bean items would be better deep fried.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews: Long time eat the watercress soup noodle in Causeway point, overall still as good. Can add pork lards is plus point. Service also ok. Didn't know got yong toufu set. Better than kok kee i feel. Added abalone stick overall $10.40

Edit: I usually come at 6

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews: Went for dinner on 21/02/26 at 6.40pm at their outlet at Toa Payoh Cebtral foodcourt. Human hair spotted on the cutlery container. Chilli and cutlery running low and not refilled.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews: 4 cursed workers (1 female & 3 male) at the counter on 18 Feb at 1124hrs were extremely rude. They thought of themselves, delayed my takeaway order by 17mins without apologies. Poor owner Burnt salary to them to make them chase away regular customers.

Restaurant Name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken (Toa Payoh 500)
Reviews:
I’ve been a fan of Lam’s for years, especially their salt-baked chicken, but my visit today was extremely disappointing. For the first time in all my years of ordering Lam’s, the staff were rude and made me feel very uncomfortable.

Ordering was stressful, the lady cashier repeatedly questioned my a la carte chicken order. Then when I asked about the braised mushroom noodle (I always order this online but the menu in-store is tea flower mushroom noodle), the cashier just said “ok ok” without clarifying and cut me off to choose the noodle.

When I collected my order, the man with glasses handed it over in a dismissive manner. The cashier shook her head and then they both laughed in a way that made me very uncomfortable. When I asked for extra chili, the man responded with sarcastic-sounding “ok”s before finally giving it to me and then they laughed again. I’ve ordered here several times and know him as a polite and patient person based on my previous encounters.

Being treated this way was very upsetting and disappointing. I wouldn’t expect any customer to be treated like this.
High price, less portion

Not too bad.... Cant really say they deserve a 5 stars, but for a mixed vege rice, the only one Ard this area, I think it's good value (esp if U have the 10% for working there).
The food was above average for sure, but nothing fantastic. But as a daily meal, this is worth a thought.
Only issue, their selection of food is pretty limited.
So it's probably a 7.5 out of 10, and still I have come back here over and over again.
(No pics now, but will post the next time)
All 3 of my dishes were cold. Fish cold, tofu cold, steam egg cold, terrible. Will never eat from them again.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews:
Decent soup and rice.

However, we were disappointed by what felt like a lack of transparency. The olive rice served appeared to be scraped from the bottom of the pot, with hard, chewy chunks, and it looked like plain white rice had been quietly mixed in to make up the portion. We only realised this after we got home.

We completely understand that it may have been the end of the day and supplies were running low — customers are usually very reasonable. But a simple heads-up would have been appreciated. Trying to pass it off without informing customers doesn’t feel honest.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews: The soup used to be quite oily. It's better now. If F&B entities do not heed customers' feedbacks e.g. via this channel or others, it won't be long will close shop. The one near boon lay shopping centre just closed shop.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews:
Tasty Soup. Good portion for the price. Not much qalams about it. Worth a try if u enjoy double boil soup!

Located inside FM Food Master.

Carpark (at a fee) and washroom available on site.

Place can be warm on a hot day.

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews: I bought lotus root soup and asked for no meat cos I want more lotus root. End up $7.10 soup + rice and only 3 pieces of lotus root. What a reap off!!!!!

Restaurant Name: Lao Er Herbal Soup 2 (Ah Er Soup 2)
Reviews: Probably one of the best soup in jurong west , soup had multiple layers along with ingredients. The pumpkin rice is to die for.
Curry fish head and salted egg pork ribs. 🤤 Must order!
Nice place to dine....
It is a small eating place with reasonabe good taste and good price. Cosy for family dinning oit

I had a fantastic experience at Lao Hero Kitchen. The food was absolutely delicious—everything tasted fresh and flavorful. What really stood out, though, was the service. The staff were incredibly friendly and made us feel right at home. I highly recommend checking this place out!
I'm feeling sick that's why I'm taking these. The boss are very friendly, I knew them very well.

If u want to have good quality soups but hate sweating out eating at hawker centres/ coffee shops… this is the plc.
It offers a variety of good, wholesome boiled soups in a spacious aircon seatings.
Ordered the lotus root peanut soup. The soup was good, and it’s not too salty. (For those want it more salty, can add to taste at your preference)
The pumpkin rice was soft and nice too.

Will be back to try their other soups in future.

Decent lunch at Star Vista with fuss free set lunches. About $17 per pax. The soups are warm and very nice, and allows for one time refill.

The dishes are really not their specialty.
Food was great. The service was quick and the place is well air conditioned

Lao Huo Tang. Franchise with 10 stores island-wide. Set lunch $69 and three tea, with total cost $89.81 (after GST & service charge). Soup was well boiled, with soft meat. Prawn was not as nice. 辣子鸡was good.

Plenty of tables in this restaurant. Arrived at 11.45 am and got a good table.

My favourite Mee Hoon kueh in the north area. Used to come on Saturdays for lunch and always order dried mee hoon kueh with extra vegetables and fried fish on the side.
Since July, they now open until 8pm.
The evening shift is managed by younger duo and I’ve been here for dinner 3 times since. All 3 times, I found the evening kueh to be a bit too thick and not cooked thoroughly, leaving this raw flour dough taste. Will try and see if I could request it to be thinner the next time, or maybe just stick to coming back on Saturday afternoons.

Atmosphere: Can be a bit stuffy at times, especially in the afternoon. There are 80s-90s songs being played in the evening sometimes, which is a vibe I enjoy.

Update: They're no longer open in the evening.
Fried fish soup was worth the price and delicious too. Nice and crispy. Not sure why the rating is so low. Def try the fried fish or the seafood soup. Cant comment on the ban mian tho!

Use to like their food very much. Always come with friend n family. But prices had gone up alot. I don't mind if the food is still good but disappointed. And their attitude and service is very bad especially their younger generation.
Overpriced fish soup... For a bowl of fish soup : $9
Bad attitude, uncooked dough, never buying again

Tried Lao San Dry Traditional Prawn Noodle with spice for the second time and I really like it! The noodles were cooked just right — not overly soft — and the flavour wasn’t too salty. The soup on the side was really good too, super rich and comforting. Definitely a satisfying bowl!
Terrible service by the lady preparing the noodles. I didn't have smaller change other than $50 and she berated me like she owes me a living. Do not patronise.
Bought prawn noodle soup. Their soup portion is very pathetic. I don’t know how that is considered as soup.

Super bad experience. I wanted to add some chilli padi. The guy told me they use sambal. So I told him about the chilli padi inside the soy sauce container. I was scooping here and there because there wasn’t much left. After I’m done, guess what, he opened the freaking fridge, took out a freaking container of chilli padi, and freaking refilled the soy sauce container with full of chilli padi. I told him that he could have put some in my container and he just brushed me off. When he was putting my container into a plastic bag, I told him it’s ok, he looked at me, continued whatever he was doing, I told him again it’s ok, he continued whatever he was doing, and handled it to me in plastic bag.

Also, they don’t give u any soup in plastic bag. You have to pay for container or bring your own container.

I swear I will NEVER return again.

Ordered intestine noodles add prawn. $2 for the prawns and just 1 min later, forget to add my prawns in. Came home to realize it’s prawn-less. Soup pic - paid a dollar for extra soup takeaway and only half a container. Cashier Msian, cook China here in Spore work but both can’t speak English at all.
Great place to find all type of good food for an affordable price. The vibe is also super nice.
Food not good

It's a very cool place to visit as a tourist, but honestly everything we tried was disgusting.
Special mention to Habib's Express, which also had terrible service

Great selection of food from multiple vendors.

We got there around 2:30 pm and just missed the lunch rush. It appeared that some of the vendors were already closed and others simply exhausted.

We had bites from two different vendors and both were very good.

We couldnt seem to find napkins and had to clean tables before we sat down. Some vendors did not sell drinks, but we did find Tiger beer.

Glad we stopped by!

Restaurant Name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
Reviews: In Alexandra Village Hawker. Next to the famous avocado drink stall. Decent plate of charsiew rice. The sauce is very different from most stores. Savory rather than sweet

Restaurant Name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
Reviews: One of the best roasted meats in the business, so don’t be deceived by the presentation. The sauce is savoury and not too sweet which is excellent.

Restaurant Name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
Reviews: チャーシューライスの認識が変わるほど美味い！オススメは叉焼焼肉飯、独特のタレがクセになる。チリを少し混ぜると旨さ倍増😇1人でもスモールサイズでは無く、中以上のサイズを頼んだほうが幸せになれる！皿の色が最近緑色からオレンジに変わった模様。ずっと緑色だったので、なんとなく違和感がある💦

(Update: This stall will permanently close by the end of June 2026 as there are not enough customers to keep the business going due to low footfall at the coffeeshop.
(The much-raved ‘Oh My Don’ Japanese stall at the same coffeeshop has already shut due to this)
So best enjoy the food before this stall shuts permanently!)

Unlike other zi char stalls, this stall sells a healthier and more wholesome selection of dishes that one doesn’t feel ‘jelak’ after eating.

Besides a choice of different styles of steam fish, it also sells a lot of other delicious healthy steamed dishes as well such as steamed prawns, steamed pork ribs in black bean sauce, black fungus steamed chicken, steamed egg, steamed otah.

There are plenty of other dishes too like Curry fish head, curry fish meat and some Zi Char dishes like prawn paste chicken, different styles of fried rice, San lor hor fun, stir fried Nai Bai with garlic, onion ginger fish slices, etc.

Although not on the menu, customers can ask for a smaller portion of a particular dish with rice, eg 姜葱鱼片饭 and they will charge accordingly like $7.

$3.50 Budget Meal is Egg Fried Rice.
Open for both lunch and dinner.
Close on Tuesday

The food.. wooo! The reason why I’m here.. unmatched. Must try! Uncle is very polite and brings warm not just in serving but the taste of the food. Price is reasonable. Place is peaceful and convenient with car park above the eatery. Had a hearty meal before another round of CNY reunion.

Food served were fresh and nice taste. Ordered the beancurb, slice steam fish, prawn paste chicken, nai Bai, steam otah. The dishes were prepared with less oil and salt with taste. I quite enjoyed the food.
Fish and prawns ingredients are fresh in the dishes sold by this store

San lau hor fan and steam fish really slaps, curry fish slice also slaps.

Kudos!

Nice, delicious food, forgot to take pics as couldn’t wait to dig in
Food is really good!

Don’t know what’s up with the other reviews but the chicken rice here is super solid. I would call it a little slice of French heaven!
We tried Bobo and Londoniene from the menu. Impeccable quality! Especially the granolas ❤️ The ambience was cozy and aesthetic.
The food was exceptional and the people were even better. Truly welcoming!
It has to be one of the best experiences of my Singapore visit.

First time ordering via Grab.
I chose the avocado toast based on the photos, and the rest of the menu looked promising.

When the order arrived, I was genuinely surprised to receive half a slice of avocado toast. The menu clearly shows a full slice of sourdough, so this felt misleading.

I reached out to the restaurant via Grab chat, but received no response.

For context, the order included tea, orange juice, and a small granola with fruit, totalling SGD 27. At that price point, receiving only half a slice of avocado toast is disappointing.

The issue here isn’t just portion size, it’s accuracy. If the product doesn’t match what’s advertised, it creates a sense of mistrust.

Overall, a disappointing experience. Not quite what you’d expect.
Love the food, coffee and kids meal here. It feels peaceful sitting outside

I also often crave their ikan bilis porridge, and homemade soy milk cos it's not sweetened and thick - makes a great local breakfast. Be sure not to miss their hawthorn (San-cha) jelly - the one and only place I've been able to find this.
Food tastes nostalgic, simple and homecooked. The tomyum soup reminds you of the food you had back at the canteen in primary and secondary school.

Thumbs up and our praises for Le tian tian as they never fail to impress with their food taste and professionalism! My recent excursion to Mad Charcoal during the sun-drenched lunch hour proved to be more than a mere meal; it was a masterclass in the delicate choreography between fire and freshness.

The plate arrived with an architectural grace that belied its rustic origins. Resting atop a dark, leaf-shaped vessel, the Pork Belly sat in a triumphant row of golden-brown tiles. Beside it, a verdant sprawl of romaine, punctuated by the ruby-red arc of tomato wedges and the golden shards of what appeared to be crisp beancurd skin, offered a vibrant visual counterpoint.

One does not simply eat this pork; one experiences the Maillard reaction in its most evolved state. The skin boasted a glass-like shatter, yielding to a layer of rendered fat that possessed a velvety mouthfeel, nearly liquifying upon contact. The meat itself remained impeccably succulent, whispering of a long, disciplined roast that preserved its structural integrity while infusing it with a deep, umami-rich soul. The subtle, char-kissed aroma lingering on the palate provided a haunting reminder of the charcoal’s transformative power.

To find such technical proficiency at a lunchtime special price point feels almost like a heist. While the evening service may offer a more lingering ambiance, the midday experience at Mad Charcoal is a streamlined, high-octane celebration of smoke and seasoning. It is proof that high-caliber culinary execution need not always come with a staggering premium.
