Despite the relatively weak start, the pork ribs were a complete 180. They were quite literally "fall off the bone" tender and were simply delicious. I personally found the honey mustard flavour to be a tad too sweet to my liking and honestly preferred the Signature Original and Hickory flavours more. Nevertheless, if you're looking for a plate of excellent ribs, I can wholeheartedly recommend them.

Wanting to end off the meal with a dessert, we ordered a variety which included the Bro Bruce Browned Butter Brownie and the Belgian Waffles. The brownie was great, the waffle on the other hand was quite disappointing.

All in all, I would definitely still recommend this place just on the strength of the ribs alone.

Last but not least, the seafood paella for 2 pas was good. Full of flavour, and it’s not too dry or wet. The only thing I’d like is that for someone who doesn’t like peeling seafood, you might find the clams is a bit too much as you will have to dig out rice from the shells. The prawns served were fresh, but and juicy.

I would love it that they would also offer service to refil water for us. I thought it was a bit weird considering that the time we went weren’t really a peak time yet. But overall, I would come again for some Abuealita’s food.

The Mountbatten Bar & Grill at the British Club is an excellent restaurant that combines refined dining, warm hospitality, and a peaceful atmosphere. It’s quiet and elegant, making it an ideal spot to enjoy a relaxing meal. The staff are exceptionally friendly and attentive, always serving with genuine smiles and ensuring every guest feels well taken care of.

The food is consistently outstanding, from starters to desserts. The MBT Signature Truffle Focaccia is soft, fragrant, and infused with the rich aroma of truffle — a perfect start to the meal. The Traditional French Onion Soup is another highlight, deeply flavorful with a rich, slow-cooked broth and topped with Emmentaler and Gruyère toast that adds just the right balance of saltiness and creaminess. The Grilled Ibérico Pork Neck is beautifully cooked — tender, juicy, and full of natural flavor, showing great attention to detail in preparation.

The true showstopper, however, is the Crêpe Suzette. This dessert is not only delicious but also a delightful performance. The staff prepare and cook it right in front of you on a rolling cart, explaining each step and ingredient along the way. The orange juice used is freshly squeezed from real oranges, giving the sauce a vibrant, natural sweetness and aroma. Combined with butter, sugar, and liqueur, it creates a thick, glossy orange sauce that coats the delicate crêpes perfectly. The result is fantastic — warm, fragrant, and bursting with citrus flavor.

Overall, the Mountbatten Bar & Grill offers an exceptional dining experience within the British Club — delicious food, attentive service, and a serene atmosphere. It’s a wonderful choice for both special occasions and quiet, indulgent dinners.

The Mountbatten Room at the British Club Singapore exudes an air of refined elegance and historical significance. Named after Lord Louis Mountbatten, the last British Viceroy of India and a key figure in Singapore's post-war history, the room pays homage to its namesake with a tasteful blend of colonial charm and contemporary sophistication.

The upmarket restaurant serves as a versatile venue, hosting a myriad of events ranging from formal dinners and business gatherings to cultural celebrations. With its panoramic windows overlooking lush greenery, the Mountbatten Room seamlessly integrates the club's British legacy with Singapore's tropical landscape.

Whether savoring a traditional British high tea or engaging in lively conversations during social events, visitors to the Mountbatten Room experience a curated blend of nostalgia and contemporary luxury. It stands as a testament to the enduring connection between the British Club and Singapore's historical tapestry, providing a distinguished setting for both reflection and celebration.

Finally made it to Naked Finn, a seafood spot I first noticed more than a decade ago when it was just a humble roadside shack in Gillman Barracks. Since then, it has evolved into a sleeker, more polished space just a stone’s throw away, without losing its soul. The trek down was well worth it – the seafood here is all about pristine freshness and precise, respectful cooking - a nod to the "Naked" in its name.

A zesty chilled beehoon crowned with crisp sakura ebi set the tone: bright, refreshing, and perked up by a punchy sambal that made for a super additive starter; we had to have seconds. The sugarloaf cabbage arrived beautifully charred and naturally sweet, lavishly cloaked in rich anchovy butter.

The undisputed star of the evening was the Soon Hock – a whole marble goby, deep-fried with its scales on so the skin turned shatteringly crisp, the flesh beneath moist and delicately sweet, lounging in a pool of light soy sauce. It’s a dish that perfectly encapsulates the kitchen’s quiet mastery of seafood.

For something more substantial, the Donabe is a no-brainer: this evening’s version featured a fillet of Madara, a flaky Pacific cod, nestled atop fluffy Koshihikari rice that soaked up all the savoury juices. Desserts kept to the same thoughtful, unfussy spirit: a house-made chendol and Thai red ruby with coconut sorbet provided a cool, nostalgic finish.

All of this was wrapped in top-shelf service – warm, genuinely friendly, and backed by authoritative knowledge of where every ingredient comes from – making for a casual yet refined seafood dinner that feels special without ever trying too hard.

Newton Food Center is often touted as a 'must visit' for tourists in Singapore and, unfortunately, this results in high footfall despite the experience warranting it.

The food is quite okay-okay. Nothing spectacular, just run of the mill hawker food at above average prices.

The main issue is that the hawker uncles/aunties seem to be a bit more 'sales-y' and pushy than other hawkers. In most other hawker centers in Singapore, they would simply leave you be (unless you have questions to ask) and if you should wish to purchase, you may approach the stall. At Newton Food Center, the staff are constantly trying to sell to you when you are wandering around browsing. This is called 'touting' and its not part of the usual hawker experience but happens too often in Newton Food Center. This makes the experience far less pleasant as you have to ignore and avoid eye contact and reflects poorly on Singapore and our hawker culture to tourists who come to visit us and wish to experience our hawker culture first hand.

There was also an issue of some stalls trying to effectively 'monopolize' the tables near their stall. How it's supposed to work in Singapore hawker centers is that you simply sit at any available seat in the hawker center, purchase your food from any stall you choose, and enjoy your food. However, when me and my friends found a table near a stall, the stallowner came to us trying to 'sell' us drinks or food. Although he didn't persist, it was an uncomfortable experience and not what hawker culture in Singapore is about.

As a general rule of thumb, good food doesn't need to be 'pushed' or 'sold'- it sells itself! Tourists are recommended to go to other hawkers like Old Airport Hawker for a more true and authentic hawker experience.

🟢 Ambience / Decor
************************
🟢 Oasis at The Grand Hyatt is a dedicated poolside restaurant and bar located by the hotel's swimming pool deck. It has both alfresco seats and indoor ( air con) seats too.

🟢 We came here for the ala carte menu as I prefer eating local Singapore dishes.

🟢 The Oasis restaurant is set in the midst of this spectacular rainforest landscape & lush waterfall area.🌿🌳 The entire garden lawn and the lush verdant flora and fauna are so astoundingly beautiful. ➖️  In the middle of concrete Orchard Road, you suddenly find yourself in an Amazon-like rainforest. 🟡 The Food = Dine in dishes
______________________________
🟡 Laksa Singapura SGD28 - The Filipino staff attending to us was kind enough to ask the kitchen to spilt the laksa bowl into 2 bowls for my husband and myself. ▪︎I also requested deshelled tiger prawns, and the chefs kindly peeled the prawns for us. So grateful. 🙏🏻

🟡 The Laksa at Hyatt Hotel reminded me of the delicious Nonya Laksa my late Peranakan mum used to cook for us. The laksa broth was creamy and full of umami flavour. The prawns were fresh and succulent.

🟠 Mee Goreng / SGD28
**************************
🟠 The Mee Goreng here is simply scrumptious — an upmarket, refined take on our familiar hawker classic. The noodles were springy & well tossed in a fragrant, savoury-sweet sauce, with a deeper, more balanced flavour profile and less greasiness than the usual street-style version.

🟠 Ingredients tasted fresher and more premium, giving the dish a cleaner & lighter finish. Familiar in taste, yet elevated and restaurant-style.

🟣 Service = A shout-out to Ms Sujeong, the Korean Senior Team Leader.➖️ She attended to us during payment time and I had a short chat with her. ▪︎Sujeong informed us about the changes to the poolside and restaurant area at ( Level 1 Terrace Wing) when Hyatt hotel was being renovated for 3 years from 2022 till mid-2025.

🟣 Sujeong was gracious, affable and polite. ● It is really nice to meet staff like that who are genuine in their demeanour and you can tell the Hyatt Oasis staff all takes great pride in their work.

🟣 I will be back soon to dine at Oasis again. Because I truly love the rainforest dining experience! 🌳🌳🌿 The whole setting felt almost surreal — like stepping into a tropical garden oasis right in the middle of busy Orchard Road.

If you’re in Singapore and want the classic chili crab experience with a postcard view of Marina Bay, this place will absolutely deliver. The chili crab itself was good. Rich sauce, fresh crab, plenty messy in the way chili crab should be. That said, the price made us blink a bit. It’s one of those meals where halfway through you look at the bill and think, “Well… I guess we’re paying for the view tonight.”

Beyond the crab, we actually found better value in the rest of the menu. The pork ribs were excellent and the fried rice was solid comfort food after wrestling with the crab. The bao buns were perfect for soaking up that chili sauce too. Owners and managers were warm and welcoming, though the rest of the service felt more assembly line than hospitality. Not rude, just very efficient and a bit impersonal.

Overall I’d call this a generous 4 out of 5. It leans touristy and very expensive, but that doesn’t automatically make it bad. If you want the chili crab “experience” with Marina Bay glowing in the background, it checks the box nicely. Time your reservation to the Marina Bay Sands light show and you’ll at least feel like the scenery helped justify the bill.

Would I rush back? Probably not. We tried chili crab a couple times in Singapore and this was the best version we had, but it’s still a $150–$200 per person novelty dinner. Fun to do once, great views, mediocre service, and a reminder that sometimes the sauce is cheaper than the scenery.

Poh Poh Roasted Chicken Rice sits quietly in the far reaches of Teban Gardens Food Centre, a place few would visit unless they live or work nearby. Yet this unassuming stall rewards anyone who makes the trip. Although Google Maps lists its hours as 7.30am to 8.30pm, the owners were still preparing when I first arrived and mentioned they would be ready at 10am. I returned later in the afternoon at 4pm, when only a small handful of stalls were open, and Poh Poh was among the few serving at that hour.

The steamed chicken had already sold out for the day, a good sign of its popularity, so I ordered the roasted chicken rice. Portions come in two sizes at $4 and $5, with an optional egg for an additional dollar. The owners were warm and generous, even encouraging me to come back for more rice if I was still hungry. A simple bowl of soup accompanied the dish.

The serving was hearty and satisfying. The roasted chicken was tender with a pleasant smokiness, the rice fragrant and well-seasoned, and the overall plate comforting in its simplicity. If anything could be improved, it would be the soup, which felt more functional than distinctive. Still, the meal was enjoyable and filling, and Poh Poh stands out as one of the better chicken rice options in the Teban Gardens area.

I look forward to returning to try the crispy pork next tim

After trying the Western food and the Indonesian fried chicken at Rasa Rasa @ Yishun, I was quite satisfied with the food quality and service. However, that completely changed today after I tried the chicken rice stall there.
At lunchtime today, I went to the chicken rice stall and asked for a takeaway chicken rice with two chicken wings and chicken gizzard. Yes, it is really that simple and easy to understand. Yet the Chinese staff member taking the order took almost five minutes just to understand what I wanted. I am not new to ordering chicken rice — at other stalls, whether Halal or non-Halal, they understand immediately. I really don’t understand why communication at this stall was so difficult.
Even the Chinese staff member chopping the chicken beside him had already understood what I wanted, yet the one taking the order remained totally confused and only got more and more lost.
Then came the most unbelievable part. I was told that the price for my order had to be calculated as follows:
•	Chicken rice with one wing: $6
•	Extra chicken meat (because the second wing must be counted this way): $5
•	Chicken gizzard: $1.80
•	Two takeaway boxes: $0.60
Total: $13.40
For a simple request of two chicken wings, I was forced to pay an additional $5 for extra chicken meat, which felt like a form of forced upselling. I reluctantly accepted it.
But the shocking part came when the food was prepared. The “extra chicken” turned out to be dry, skinless chicken breast — completely white, with no fat and extremely tough in texture.
As for the chicken gizzard, the staff took out a box of pre-sliced gizzards from the refrigerator — clearly frozen leftovers from the previous day. Anyone who knows food safety understands that offal spoils very easily. Yet they were selling overnight frozen gizzards. In my decades of eating chicken rice in Singapore, this is the first time I have ever seen chicken offal that is not freshly sliced on the spot.
Compared to other chicken rice stalls that usually cost under $10, here I paid a much higher price while also having to worry about food safety risks.
This chicken rice stall has now moved straight to the top of my “never return” list. I will also make sure to alert nearby residents online about this experience.

PS：

If you’re visiting Bali and craving an authentic, high-quality seafood experience, Bali Nikmat in Kuta is an absolute must-visit. From the moment you pull up to the restaurant—easily recognizable by its iconic giant crab sign—you know you’re in for a treat. This establishment has been a staple since 2000, and it’s easy to see why it has maintained such a stellar reputation for over two decades.

The atmosphere is classic and bustling, perfectly capturing that "old-school" Chinese restaurant charm. It’s the kind of place that feels lively and welcoming, making it ideal for large family gatherings or a feast with friends. Despite how busy it gets, the service remains impressively efficient and attentive, ensuring that you’re never waiting too long for your next course.

Now, let’s talk about the food, which is the real star of the show. The seafood here is exceptionally fresh, likely because they specialize in live catches. We ordered the Creamy Salted Egg Crab, and it was life-changing. The sauce was rich, velvety, and perfectly seasoned, clinging to the succulent, sweet crab meat. It is arguably the best version of this dish on the entire island. We also tried the Fried Garlic Butter Prawns, which were crispy on the outside and incredibly juicy on the inside, packed with aromatic garlic flavor.

Another standout was the Steamed Live Fish with Soy Sauce. The fish was steamed to perfection—flaky and delicate—while the light soy dressing enhanced the natural sweetness of the seafood without overpowering it. Even the side dishes, like the stir-fried kailan with garlic, were executed with precision, providing a fresh and crunchy balance to the rich seafood mains.

While it is a Chinese-style restaurant, the flavors are elevated and distinctly premium. The portions are generous, and though it’s a "bustling spot," the quality of the ingredients justifies every bit of the price. Whether you are a local or a tourist, Bali Nikmat delivers a consistent, world-class dining experience. I’ve been to many seafood spots in Bali, but I keep coming back here because the flavors are simply unmatched. Five stars all the way—don’t leave Bali without eating here!

Chilli - i request to have the chilli to contain in the small bowl , the uncle say use the plastic saucer will do , i say i want small bowl, he side stare me sia .. walao dont gey gao chilli la i is got eat the chilli one , not take and look de .. 😒

Secondly , clearly the outlet is understaff , when we reach , there were only 1-2 table having mookata , so i reckon the other staff is busy for online orders , our mookata took close to 25 mins and the item came in separate order manner . Uncle is impatience , but maybe he is like that one la but … u cannot shout back or pek cek back at customer one ma unless the customer make u pek cek first.. but you all the way pek cek one leh .. order never come i also dont dare ask .. our fire no more liao u ask us wait .. den we wait more than 5 mins , u ask us wait again .. peng kang food can wait de meh .. sigh ..

Lastly, you have 2 -3 staffs handle multiple companies order meh? One cook porridge, one cook thai food, one handle mookata..

Siam Square management , please provide more staff for this outlet , i believe happy staff will make customer makan session enjoyable also.

Too many reviews of this place that speaks of the legendary rude staff. Took too long to prepare the food. When approached, he spoke in his own mother tougue. I don't blame him when he's the only one manning the store, preparing porridges for another stall. The management... 🤦‍♂️

I was at Siam Square Mookata Jurong West outlet at around 6.36pm today. After waiting for 20 minutes with no dishes served, I went to check with the person in charge. I understand it was peak hour, but when I asked how much longer we needed to wait, he replied to me in Chinese: “你要吃就吃，不要吃就走.”

Is this really how your staff are trained to speak to customers? This attitude is completely unacceptable. Siam Square Mookata has always been one of my favourite places, but after this experience, I’m very disappointed and I don’t think I will be supporting anymore.
It has undergone renovations. The price is still affordable and the food delicious.
Affordable price for Mookata, opens till late and my friends love to gather here.

Saw a kid take ice cream from the tub, put it into her mouth, then scoop again into the same tub. I informed the staff, but no action was taken to replace or remove the ice cream. This is very unhygienic and disappointing, hope the management can take food safety more seriously.

Always come here for supper. Recently noticed the price is so expensive nowadays costed me $25 per pax- with little given… cost price for meat shouldn’t be that much please give at least 2-3 pcs of pork more i counted only 5 small slices for $3.60 which i can easily buy outside. I understand that with recent rental hikes it’s expensive but please be reasonable too

do not order the miniature prawn paste. $3.60 for this????

Edit: managed to split it up into 6 very very small pieces. Each small piece is $0.60 :)))))) refer to pic below
Meat big cut... Hard to grill, always short of dish. Say miss. After food come must count. Cannot trust.

The broccoli was not fresh and looked black, the rice was hard and dry, and some items we ordered were not served. The service was also poor, yet we were still charged a 10% service fee. Very disappointing overall — I will not be going back again.

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata In Singapore)
Reviews: Craving for Mookata... Nowadays Mookata buffet alot in Singapore but we need quality not quantity. So we come over there their meat is well seasonal it garlic pork belly and black pepper pork belly so tasty... We spend $66 yes is more expensive then buffet Mookata but we have it in quality.....

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata In Singapore)
Reviews:
Recently visited Siam Square Mookata at Golden Mile Tower, and it was a great experience! The marinated meats were fresh, flavorful, and grilled perfectly. The dipping sauce was the real star—super tasty and complemented the BBQ so well.
I like that they have multiple outlets, making it convenient to enjoy their food in different locations. The vibe is casual and fun, perfect for gathering with friends or family over a hearty meal.

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Upper Thomson)
Reviews: I ate here on a quiet Sunday, had a fantastic service from Dung, strongly recommend!

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Upper Thomson)
Reviews: On CNY Eve we prepared a feast for our family but was missing the butane fuel canister to cook the hotpot. FairPrice and Shengsiong was closed, 7-11 and other convenience stores didn’t carry any. I walked by this restaurant and asked to buy 2 canisters, and the 2 sweet Thai staff gave it to me without question and refused to take my money, effectively saving our reunion dinner. They honestly made me feel lucky! I came back days later with 2 canisters and a small gift to them (one of the sweet staff was out buying stuff). Seriously we need to see our migrant workers as the backbone of our society, and a blessing to all. Thank you!

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Upper Thomson)
Reviews:
We planned to get a late-night mookata snack on a whim, just the two of us. We thought it’d be a cheap and cheerful meal—we were told the buffet was over $30 ➕➕
per person, but the final bill came to a whopping $130 total 🥲

We asked if they had an à la carte option when we walked in, and the staff said yes. Then my husband decided to switch to the buffet instead.

First, they handed us an à la carte bill for $112. I was shocked and pointed out we’d had the buffet, not à la carte. The staff looked dismissive, then reprinted a buffet bill—which was even more expensive at $130. And they refused to switch back to the $112 bill, claiming they’d printed too many receipts already.

To make it worse, the buffet didn’t include all dishes—some items were extra charge, and the staff never bothered to mention that. I even had to ask if water was included with the buffet because they didn’t say a word about it. The staff spent most of the time on their phones since it was quiet late at night, with zero proper communication.

And when I checked the receipt at home? They charged us for 3 bottles of Coke Zero when we only had 2. Seriously, what were they even doing at work?

This was our first time here, and it’ll definitely be the last. For $130, we could’ve had way better hot pot or BBQ with actual service. Lesson learned with buffets: ask every single detail before you order. Sure, we could’ve been more thorough—but the restaurant’s service and staff accountability need a massive upgrade.

Avoid this place at all costs:
SIAM SQUARE MOOKATA (UPPER THOMSON)

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Upper Thomson)
Reviews:
One of the best mookata but today a bit disappointed with the pork collar. Almost all fat n no meat.
But staff helped to cancel my pork collar order. Will still come back cos it’s tasty n price reasonable.

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Upper Thomson)
Reviews:
Been here two times, both times with my children. One time tried Ala Carte, one time try buffet.
Both are good value for money— depending on their appetites!
Meats are well marinated and thinly sliced, prawns are big and fresh. Generous amounts of vegetables.

Drinks to buy separately, as are some premium ingredients.

Attentive service.
Chili and sauces self service.
Ice cream also included!

Washroom is clean.

Will definitely be back

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Bukit Batok Street 11)
Reviews: The food quality is not good and not fresh at all. The prices are charged higher than other branches. And this is the WORST Siam Square Mookata I've eaten. The worst is the terrible services from a young man and old auntie, both have really stuck up faces and extreme rude attitude towards us. No more next time.

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Bukit Batok Street 11)
Reviews: food was served fast, food was great and they give free ice cream!!

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Bukit Batok Street 11)
Reviews:
Terrible service despite decent food.
I’ve been to Siam Square Mookata a few times and the food is generally good, but my recent experience was unacceptable. We ordered a normal plate of garlic chicken, but they served a large plate instead. When we checked the bill, they had changed our order in the system and charged us almost triple the price.

When we raised this to the cashier, she didn’t care at all. Her exact attitude was basically, “so what, you guys already ate it.” No apology, no explanation, nothing. Just pure rudeness and zero accountability.

Restaurant Name: Siam Square Mookata (Best Mookata Restaurant In Singapore) (Bukit Batok Street 11)
Reviews:
Reached around 10.15pm, and by 11pm the lights and fans were switched off. It was extremely hot, and with only the dim lighting from the sidewalk, it was almost impossible to see if the food was even cooked properly.

The grill plate was dirty, and the table hadn’t been wiped clean either. For $32.90/pax (buffet, without drinks), the standard was shockingly poor. Food choices were very limited, mostly cheap frozen items. Some weren’t even fresh, which completely killed my appetite.

To make things worse, I went home straight after and ended up with a bad stomach.

Overall, the dining experience was terrible. At this price point, it is absolutely not worth it. Anyone considering this buffet is better off skipping it—I definitely will not be returning.
I said no spicy. The stall still go ahead and give me spicy. Very long wait too. Very disappointing.
Delicious and yummy Thai food with good service from the staff, reasonable price for the taste and portion ⭐️🌟💫✨

Worst bcm ever
Order for breakfast but the noodle is legi tasteless.Order with chill but no taste at all noodle does not have any sauce at all also
Soup taste kind of salty. Liver is overcook and very hard. Not worth the 5 buck to eat. Topping also very little. Eat once not coming back again
Most vibes noodle bar
Natural and eco friendly place. Staff are attentive.
Steak was very good. Staff very honest and returned my bat and run after me. Thank y so much
Great place! Staff were amazing! Very sweet and helpful.. hearty and modestly priced food at Sentosa :)

This place has always been a happy little getaway for us that's always left us with fond memories on our anniversary celebrations.

This year, marking our 10th, was no different. Warm smiles, professional demeanours and excellent food made feel just as welcome as we did the first time we decided to pop down for breakfast.

Special shout out to Sasi, Nabil and Rebecca for their exceptional service; always super attentive to each guests needs and never dismissive no matter how nonsensical the questions may be (we definitely had a couple of them 😂). Really made the occasion feel extra special during a much needed break.

Quite possibly the best breakfast buffet I’ve ever had. We travel often, and this spread truly impressed authentic dishes from around the world and everything tasted great. The service was also top-notch. Definitely a breakfast experience worth having.

Beware they sell defrosted old bread. Crust is chewy and old, center cold and dense even though it was bought in the morning. It’s not the first time that I have been caught out and it is awful. Stop doing this please as a business, as we are paying a premium and expect quality of freshly-baked daily. We are able to tell the difference so stop trying to deceive your customers. Standards have been strange since their big price hike.

Update: Saw on 8 March, the staff going next door and coming back with bunches of Dole bananas from Cold Storage and with a receipt. Capitalism at its finest - buying from the neighbouring supermarket to resell at the cafe.

Food is nice enough, just that sandwich and sticky bun portions have been noticeably shrinking and prices increasing over the years which is a bummer from a paying customer POV. The service staff here are almost always grouchy/rather unwilling to serve with a smile and you often need to ask them to wipe down the tables - the only time they are noticeably in a good mood is when they are chit-chatting among themselves. Another sore point is the cafe can get extremely and unbearable noisy to the point I have to use earbuds given that they now make the bread in-house here, and loud, noisy financial advisers (and even one religious preacher) like to talk shop with elderly customers. You will also occasionally see mynahs coming into the shop. One time I even saw a bird eating off a woman's plate and I tried to chase it away, and she turned around in horror and shrieked. I can only hope noise levels can be reduced or dealt with through better sound insulation and food portions restored to their former glory and service staff who actually enjoy the service industry work here.

Haven’t had breakfast here in a while but wow, the sour dough with eggs & mushrooms are very well done plus good strong coffee.  I also think their croissants are excellent. A simple place with freshly prepared food done on site, regular go-to for those living in the neighbourhood.

Probably a running scam done by the store of staff.

Asked for Peha(Thigh) but had to pay 5.50 instead of the written price.

Staff said thigh and peha is different. dont understand what she means also. Think its a Scam by the staff to pocket some of the money. Seemed nervous when asked her to explain the difference
They have improved significantly since a few complaints. Taste is good. Service is better.

1. Staff don't know what is gizzard? I'm puzzled.

2. Waiting time is extremely long, possibly the slowest chicken rice to be served in Singapore, even Chatterbox serves faster.

3. Ayam Penyet's chicken tasted overnight and refried, kind of nonsense for $7.80.

4. More and more stuffs can't finish.

Cashier cant even speak or understand simple basic English... Hello?  Youre in Singapore in case you forgot. English has always been the 1st language. Nothing has changed. Pls send them for basic English classes.
Amazing congee. I tried the surrounding porridge, this is the best. Do try this store if you are craving some comfort food
Tried the Yishun outlet for the 1st time. Comparable to the Hougang outlet. Good!

Update: note the closing hrs for 2026 CNY (16 - 21 Feb)

Came to try porridge here. Ordered chicken porridge. It is very nice. So far, it is the best porridge that I have tried in Singapore. Nice to eat hot porridge in an air-conditioned place. Would not try this in a hot weather setting. Need to get yr own seats and seating is limited.

23 Sep 2024 Update: tried fish porridge. This is nice as well.

Ordered traditional set 1. Overall taste is ok. Eggs nicely cooked and already de shelled on behalf which is a plus point. However abit disappointed with amount of toasting and butter. Almost non-existent.
Nicely done eggs and toast. Beautiful as you can see from the photos. The Kopi o kosong is sweet itself without sugar.

here bright and early at 630am — overall great value for the quality

- tea c kosong was warm and rich with subtle sweetness
- half boiled eggs were perfect, not undercooked nor overcooked, imo better than Yakun
- bun was good (toasted for you)
- lady at store was polite and patient
- turnaround was quick, there were two folks infront of me but i got mine within 5 mins (needed to toast the bread and warm the eggs)

Was surprised to find out that the traditional set was sold out when I arrived at close to 10am on a Sunday.

Thus I had the thick peanut toast instead. It took a bit longer than the other sets, but came still pretty crispy, with decent amount of spread.

Eggs were too overcooked for my liking - the yolk while still viscous, remained stuck together.

Kopi-c kosong iced was pretty good. Coffee was what you'd expect, but they did not skimp on the evaporated milk.

came on a saturday morning around 9.30am and there was a snacking queue here! tried their traditional kaya toast set & taro toast. kaya toast was thin & crispy with the right amount of kaya. eggs and kopi were all right, appreciate if the egg yolks could be runnier. taro toast was a letdown - taro spread tasted like a blend of coconut & white chocolate..? not a huge fan. props to them for the innovative idea though!

Beef Stroganoff Pasta: Delicious and fragrant sauce with the moistest and softest steak cuts! There’s also mushrooms and bell pepper, although I wish there was more bell pepper 😋The amount of sauce and the portion size were just right 👍

Salmon Pink Pasta: The salmon was also very soft and moist! Probably the best salmon I have ever tasted, it was cooked really well 😋

Tiramisu Latte (Special): Not sure what the crunchy bites on top are, but they tasted like thin biscuits and added a really nice touch to the drink! Loved the cheese foam on top — it tasted amazing!! Definitely would order this again, only served cold ❄️

Chicken Floss Seaweed Tater Tots: Can’t go wrong if you love tater tots! Great for sharing and super crispy 👍

Homemade Nougats: Can't really tell what flavours they were though but they were soft and had an interesting texture!

The lady who served us was really nice and the whole place felt very homely, loved the music choice too! it sounded like songs from the old Disney movies
Okay. Compact, nice service. Food is good
Love the food, especially the tom yum pasta and crab meat pasta. Service is fantastic too!

Excellent service. Super sweet and nice owner. Love the tofu, perfect balance of flavours, half with a delicious egg sauce half with a sweet sesame.. the flavour of the tofu still comes through, and somehow becomes 10000x tastier....

I had the k style cream chicken pasta, my girlfriend had the bacon carb, beautiful al dente noddle that was warm and hearty but never gelat. Many flavours, i love the seaweed in the k style cream chicken

Sorry no food photo. We were too locked in on eating

I was greeted n by a friendly and cheery lady boss.
Although she is busy doing closing and cleaning her stall at the end of the day, she is still cheery and energetic.

There are a few fish dishes to choose from.
I came for the Pig's Trotters!

When I sat, and started to eat, the meat was soft and tender and very delightfully tasty! Traditionally done to perfection. I savour ever drop of it. Yums!

I will be back for sure and will try the fish soup dishes.

Thank you for a wonderful experience. 😃👍🏽✨
The staff is very warm, Soup is resonably priced & loads of ingredients & fresh
Nice seafood soup

Bought  dory seafood soup. Large portion and the soup is so tasty.
I go definitely go again.

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews:
Really enjoyed the prawn cracker that is crisp and not at all oily. Pinnacle of how a really good prawn cracker ought to be!

For more details, visit 2bearbear today!

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews: I used to like this stall a lot. Have not had the food for quite a while and unfortunately I feel that the standards had declined by quite a bit. The prawn crackers were over fried and hard. The sausage was just gelatin and very little meat. Ngoh hiang had little taste. Only the chili was still good. Really do hope they can recover their original taste.

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews: One of the best Wu Xiang I have tried so far. And items are homemade. Very underrated stall. Uncle & Aunty very friendly too

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews: Been coming here for 18 years, food is not very oily and price point is just great. The prawn cracker has lots of prawn in it and has a crunch. The auntie remembers me and is always very welcoming, although I don't live near I love coming by and enjoying my childhood Ngo Hiang.

Restaurant Name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
Reviews: Ngo Hiang is not bad, the chili sauce could be stronger.
in this sin xiang kee teochew noodle stall,the foods and plain rice prices must be adjust downwards please.the plain rice must sell at 50 cent.the foods must be delivered to the customer table.

My favourite organ soup stall in Yew Tee. For a 4.50 portion, I think there are plenty of ingredients! I love the soup, brewed well and has strong 酸菜 taste. Using loin meat is great for texture, normally they would use small intestines.

Although at night if you purchase, it taste a little too concentrated. Might need to add water periodically!

The auntie’s son can be a little cranky, but he knows how to cook!

Paid $4.50 for a bowl of bak chor mee. The noodle was springy. The pork slices were tasty and tender. The pig liver and meat balls were also tender. The free pig organ soup was tasty too. Altough I asked not to add chilli sauce to the noodle, there was no ketchup or black vinegar added - very different from other bak chor mee stalls. Nevertheless, this was the best bak chor mee I have eaten in Yew Tee. Service was prompt as there was no queue.

Delicious foods 😍
Price is reasonable.
Mee Rebus is tasty. I added ladyfingers.
Food is tastless and expensive. Plus small opens whenever they feel like it. 1st and 15th day of the month also suka suka open and close. Terribly unreliable.

Sumptuous Vegetarian Lor Mee ($4.00)
Topped up an additional vegetarian Ngor Hiang (素五香) which cost another $1.50. Mom shared some green vegetables from her order w me.

Overall. It's filling. If you looking for Vegetarian food in this food centre, this is the place to patronise.

The most inedible vegetarian food ever .
Locals have the worst palate to consider this good food .

Vege esp the french beans is so saltish and msg laden .

Ladyfingers are not fully cooked hence tough .

The chinese ladies are not exactly customer friendly . And food aint that cheap either considering is all veges .
Not to mention inedible due to not fully cooked and some so saltish msg laden .

Have to throw most of it away .

* Almost choked on their food .
( not too sure whats inside the food .. plastics or what ? )

* Buy at your own risk
absolutely rude staff working at the drinks stall
Porridge is good, comparable to Chong pang market. Kolo mee is average.
The mixed rice is nice, but drink stall lady has bad attitude, they purposely fold all the table and ask me to leave if not buying any drink mentioned other people need to sit.

Had our meals as a family at this store for a few times, enjoyed our meals, love their prawn paste chicken, but today’s experience was the most outstanding of all. We approached the counter at 2:02pm, on 18/1/2026 Sunday, and was told that they are closed. The Chinese lady who serves the food and takes order who informed us of the closure, was chopping some chili near the counter. The sign says operating hours until 2:30pm, why is it that they are closed at 2pm? We are not even ordering an entire feast, we just wanted to order 2-3 dishes, but anyway, we didn’t even get to the ordering part, she straight up told us that they are closed.
Order food delivery small at sting ray ever seen and veggies like soaked in water

The zi Char is situated within a coffee shop that is slightly away from the Le Quest mall and Tengah project. There are blocks of residential coming up, so I do expect the dining crowd to increase with time.

The salted egg calamari was nice- flavourful and fried to golden crisp. Stingray was alright, the sambal lacked a punch. Portion of rice was good.

Overall, if you live nearby, this would be an option for family meals.
Food is great. Kids super love the chicken wings. The sea bass deal is worth it too.

Delightful dining at Siong BBQ Seafood. Their signature Hot Plate Stingray was delicious, with tender stingray cooked in a flavorful sambal sauce. I also enjoyed their fresh fried fish options, which were a great accompaniment to rice.

The classic Cai Po Beancurd and the flavorful Prawn Paste Fried Chicken were delicious additions to my meal.
Ordered mee soto. $5, turns out only noodles a bit of taugay. No meat at all. If you told me first, maybe I can accept, but this is terrible.
Great!
Famous for their lontong but this mee rebus is so good especially if you crave for it for supper. They still selling at after 9pm. $5.00. Fast and efficient.
Nasi Lemak was really nice, sambal was good and overall service was friendly. Will come back again

Here on travel. Didn’t bring enough cash for what I wanted and the lady offered to give me the food for free. Was taken aback from her kindness. Had enough coins to buy 1 pack so just did that. Food was very fair for the price. Would go back again based on quality of food and her kindness.

Quán nasi briyani theo mình là ngon nhất Singapore.
Gà chiên giòn, bên trong mọng nước.
Cà ri dê cũng ngon lắm.
Hạt cơm mềm, chín vừa và ráo.
Bánh tráng ăn cũng giòn.
Nghe nói quán nghỉ cũng hơi buồn.
Mình ở xa nên ít ghé.
Small little eating place. Near busy road.
The stall already closed down since Jan 2019. And is currently replace with another Briyani stall.
Great hangout for food and watching all the cars parking I small spaces to collect food.  Great fun for us.
Nice food

Old-school nasi lemak done well. Rice is fragrant with a nice texture, and the sambal has that roasted, slightly sweet flavour that keeps you eating. Chicken was a great add-on too. Simple comfort food — would recommend coming early.
Very bad service, not allowed to pick dishes and only standard sets.

One of the best signature prawn noodles with unique fish dumpling and prawn paste too. Yum Yummy 😋 Soup is awesome and very kind and nice owner n staff. Not stingy with the prawn soup. What make the prawn noodles taste different from others? Is the broth definitely! No charge for extra soup best 👍🏻 no attitude very friendly too. Best combination of delicious food and good owner and staff too 💙❤️ have been here for decades 👍🏻😊
Good bowl of dry version. But parking is shite around here.
Gonna try once next time

Best bowl of prawn noodles I’ve had in a while. Have always been a dry noodles person and typically the gee taste from the yellow noodles stands out like a sore thumb; this was not the case here - the Q of the noodles, together with the fragrance of the chilli AND the hearty soup is really comfort on a rainy day 🤤

Particular mention to the prawn paste and fish dumplings which blew my mind - totally unexpected quality of ingredients considering the price point 💯

Came here for the first time to celebrate my partner birthday, and it was definitely worth the visit!

The staffs were awesome and very friendly. The food was great and delicious. Paying a little extra for the special request was absolutely worth it, and the birthday cake was fantastic.

We would especially like to commend Mr Areon and Mr Kishore for their hospitality and service throughout the dinner. They were super friendly and professional. This is definitely one of the best restaurant service experiences we have ever had and make us want to return for sure. Truly appreciated! Please kindly convey the message to them. 💪🏻
Perfect place for a romantic birthday dinner! Thanks for the cake Skai!

My first time at SKAI Restaurant and it was a great experience. The view was amazing, especially the sunrise, and the ambiance was very relaxing and classy. The food and drinks were really good as well. It may be a bit pricey, but it’s definitely worth it for the experience.

Most of the staff were Filipino, which made the experience feel even more warm and welcoming. Special thanks to Sir Benj for taking great care of us. He was very attentive, friendly, and approachable. Overall, the staff were very nice and made our first visit memorable.” 🌅

Update February 2026:
The bar now faces North-West, so no more view of Raffles.
But it remains a stunning place.
Alas, it is poorly sign-posted from the lobby of the Swisshotel Stamford - perhaps they wish to deter non-residents.

Original review:
Of course you pay for the absolutely stunning views over the republic but they are well worth it - do try the vodkatinis.
Book a table on a clear day and arrive at around 17.30 to watch the planes landing at Changi and then the Sun go down. When the lights come out you will enjoy a very different set of vistas.
The Raffles Hotel pool below looks like a postage-stamp!
Visually the most exciting bar in the World!! We shall be back.
Nice ambience

Been years since I’m back, I would say it is an amazing experience from the service to the food. From the delicious home made sourdough and butter to their awesome appetisers and steak. Even their Cod with prawn bisque is spot on. Uni pasta is sublime. Love it , will definitely be back

Worst steakhouse I have been to. Went with kids and wife. Ordered 900g steak medium to share, mac and cheese for the kids and two sides.

1. Steak was raw and cold.
2. Sides didnt come out.
3. Service unresponsive. Fairly busy with one waiter.

Restaurant Name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh Jem
Reviews:
For some reason, I actually prefer their cheaper bak kut teh option. Even though the pork ribs have less meat, I find it tastier, but that is just my personal preference.
The soup is still very good, and a big plus point is that the refills are not diluted at all. I really enjoy it because it is very peppery, which is exactly what I look for in bak kut teh.
The sliced pork soup is alright. The pork is super soft, though I personally do not enjoy it as much because it is a bit too soft for me. Again, just personal taste.
The other side dishes are pretty normal. The sesame chicken was slightly disappointing as the sauce was too watery. I think it would be better if the sauce were thicker, although flavour wise it is still okay.
Overall, it is still a solid place for peppery bak kut teh, especially if you enjoy strong soup with unlimited refills.

Reviews:
Great place! It was darn bloody good that my family had to wait for 15 min to be seated. Can't be blamed since we went there during the peak hours. Lunch hour.

But I would like to take this opportunity to thank my wife for letting me choose lunch for the family.

The food was great! It was a shame that I didn't order more. Their kids meal was the right size for my 2 small kids. They loved their kids meal.

We we getting ourselves ready for the thinking that the seating area would be super warm since they were packed. But fortunatly the restaurant a/c held out well.

Their main dish, pork rib soup, oh~ the soup was flavourful, peppery taste, but yet, not that spicy. I was pleasantly surprised when we could ask for a refill for the soup with no additional charges. Thumbs up for that.

Usually, other restaurants/stall will reject your request and insist that you buy another serving just to taste the soup again.

The pig stomach soup is also a dish to die for! The tenderness of the meat, chewy, yet light on your jaw.

Paired with the steamy rice. O.M.G... I couldn't bear to leave the restaurant even after finishing my food. If not for my kids, I would have order another round just to stay and eat once more.

For the price we paid, it was a little expensive, but worth the taste.

Came here for dinner yesterday with my Queen and her parents. We were very hopeful for a good dinner but we went home disappointed, saying we will never visit again.

In terms of atmosphere, it gives off good vibes for a cosy Chinese cuisine dinner.

Food served and the skewers were good. The beef was way above standard. Pretty ok for the lamb and pork. The cold dish of tofu and century came after staples, it was spicy and wasn’t the sweet kind we are looking for. The pig ears with cucumbers were pure disappointment with everything gone wrong. The salted egg pumpkin was made badly, the fried pumpkin became soft and there is no crunch left. Last dish noodles were okay, they had savoury sauce over Chinese ramen.
It costed $94 for a restaurant we had too much expectations for thus we left in utter disappointment and never again.

Restaurant Name: Suki-Ya (All You Can Eat Shabu Shabu (Heartland Mall Kovan))
Reviews:
Suki-Ya at Heartland Mall Kovan is a Japanese all-you-can-eat shabu shabu restaurant that delivers generous portions, solid quality, and great value. Perfect for groups, families, or casual dinners, Suki-Ya lets you cook fresh ingredients at your table in simmering broth, choosing from two soup bases per pot to suit different tastes.

The buffet focuses on unlimited thinly sliced meats like pork and beef that cook quickly and stay tender. Orders are served fresh straight from the kitchen, keeping each serving hot and just right for tasting. Alongside the meats, there’s a self-service station with fresh vegetables, mushrooms, tofu, noodles, rice, and a variety of fish and meat balls — everything you need for a complete hotpot experience.

Sauces and condiments are easy to customise, letting you mix soy sauce, sesame, garlic, chilli, and more to match your preferred flavour profile. Most buffet packages also include unlimited soft drinks and simple desserts, offering a satisfying finish to a hearty meal.

Located inside Heartland Mall Kovan, the restaurant is easy to reach by public transport and fits well into a casual neighbourhood dining scene. The interior is straightforward and comfortable, designed to accommodate groups without fuss. Prices are affordable compared to premium hotpot spots, making this a go-to choice when you want a filling meal without overspending.

Overall, Suki-Ya at Heartland Mall Kovan is a reliable, well-priced shabu shabu buffet with fresh ingredients, friendly service, and a relaxed atmosphere.

Tea Lounge at Conrad Singapore has long been one of my dependable weekend high tea spots, so when they introduced a special Chinese New Year themed edition, I was naturally curious to see how the experience would be reimagined.

The Spread: Comforting Familiarity with Festive Twists

The generous variety that regulars appreciate remains intact. The selection is extensive without feeling overwhelming, striking a nice balance between savoury classics and playful creations.

Highlights That Stood Out
•	Seafood Congee : Easily one of the stars of the afternoon. The broth was deeply flavourful, infused with the natural sweetness of seafood, and generously topped with prawns and fish. Comforting yet refined.
•	Kurobuta Pork Char Siew : Not part of the free-flow selection, but worth every bite. Exceptionally juicy and tender, with beautifully caramelised edges that delivered a delicate crispness and smoky sweetness.
•	Quiche : Above average, featuring an impressively thin, crisp crust that avoided the heaviness many hotel versions suffer from.
•	Chicken Satay : Juicy, tender, and paired with a rich homemade peanut sauce that tasted freshly ground rather than mass-produced.

Creative Touches That Keep It Interesting

Both the sandwiches and desserts continue to be where this high tea differentiates itself from others.
•	The sandwiches showcased unexpected ingredient pairings that somehow worked harmoniously, offering pleasant surprises rather than gimmicks.
•	Desserts were particularly strong, more imaginative than those at many other hotels. The combinations of flavours and textures felt thoughtfully composed, often unconventional but consistently enjoyable.

A Small Miss
•	Singapore Laksa : Slightly underwhelming compared to the rest of the spread. The coconut milk ratio leaned too heavy, resulting in a broth that felt diluted and lacked the punchy depth one would expect.

Value for Money

At $82++ per person, it sits on the pricier end of the high tea spectrum. However, considering the quality of ingredients, execution, and the creativity shown across the menu, it still offers solid value—especially for those who appreciate a high tea that goes beyond the predictable.

Final Thoughts

This festive edition proves why I keep returning. The experience stays true to its strengths—variety, quality, and creativity—while introducing seasonal elements that make it feel refreshed rather than repetitive. It’s a reliable indulgence that still knows how to surprise.

I stumbled upon this stall ("Teochew Fishball Minced Meat Noodle" at Food Hub) and ordered their dry Fishball Minced Meat Noodles with Mee Pok.

​The Verdict:
It is very good, but you need to know what you are eating. This is NOT Bak Chor Mee (BCM); it is a proper bowl of Teochew Fishball Noodles.

​The Difference: Don't come here expecting the vinegar-forward punch or the distinct savoury depth of tee poh (dried sole fish) that defines a classic BCM. The chilli is also different—it's not the typical BCM sambal style.

​Why it's still great: Despite not being BCM, it stands on its own merits. The Mee Pok was cooked perfectly al dente—springy with a great bite. The sauce mix was flavourful and savoury, coating the noodles well.

​The Ingredients: The toppings are generous—bouncy fishballs, sliced fish cake, minced meat, and fresh crispy lard croutons (you can add more on you own, there's a box of it next to the utensils) that add a wonderful texture.

​It was so satisfying that after finishing my bowl, I immediately ordered 4 more packets to take away for my family. If you appreciate a solid, traditional Teochew Fishball noodle, this gets my stamp of approval.

Restaurant Name: The Embun Sg | Live Seafood • Ikan Bakar • Fresh Seafood (Halal)
Reviews:
I had dinner here with my family and spent almost $2,000. The food was good, but I honestly feel the price is a bit too expensive. At that price, I would expect the overall experience to better match the cost, including the service, amenities, and even the dining setup like the plates, forks, and spoons to feel more like hotel standard.

The food and drinks were okay, but to me, there was nothing very special compared to places like East Coast or other seafood restaurants. The main difference was the king crab, which stood out. Other than that, the rest felt quite normal.

I also felt that the prayer room was very small, wash basin not in working condition and not all areas were air-conditioned, which made the dining experience less comfortable.

For almost $2,000, I feel I could have gone for a buffet with a wider variety of food and desserts included. This is just my honest opinion based on the overall value and experience.

I would advise the shop to focus not only on profit, but also on making the dining experience feel worth it for families. Since many customers come with their family, it would be good to have more family set meals or value-for-money packages instead of charging separately for every single seafood item or by Kg. Of course, the business needs to make profit, but at the same time, customers should not leave feeling like they were being overcharged or ripped off. A better balance between pricing and value would make families more satisfied and more likely to return.

Seriously, I have been there once already, and I don’t think I will go back again. The price is just not worth the overall experience. I believe the shop should rethink its strategy, because customers may come once, but they may not return if they feel the value is not there.

The satay ended up tasting more fried than grilled, which was a real letdown for such a classic Singaporean dish.
Service-wise, the staff were polite and efficient enough (plates got cleared reasonably quickly), but there wasn't much warmth or enthusiasm. Smiles were few and far between, and the overall vibe felt a bit flat and unengaged compared to what you'd hope for at a place like this.

Palm Restaurant Review

*Rating:* 2.5/5

I recently had the opportunity to dine at the Palm Restaurant, located within Singapore Swimming Club. While the setting is lovely, our experience was a bit of a mixed bag.

*Ambiance:* 4/5
The restaurant's ambiance is elegant and inviting, perfect for a special occasion or a night out with friends and family.

*Food:* 4/5
The menu is impressive, offering a wide variety of dishes from local cuisines to Western favorites like pasta. We were excited to try out different options, and the food was generally delicious.

*Service:* 2/5
Unfortunately, the service was a letdown. Because reservations are not allowed, we had to arrive early to secure a table for our large group. However, once seated, we had to wait quite a while for our orders to be taken and served. The waiters seemed overwhelmed and the service was not friendly.

*Value:* 3/5
Given the quality of food and service, the prices were reasonable. However, the lack of reservations and slow service might deter some diners.

*Overall:* 2.5/5
While the Palm Restaurant has potential, the service needs significant improvement. If you're planning to visit, arrive early to secure a table, and be patient with the staff.

2. Auntie actually scooped away the cucumber.
The server initially gave what seemed like a reasonable amount of cucumber, but the auntie (presumably the owner or supervisor) told him it was “too much” and proceeded to scoop some out right in front of me. If $0.90 can’t even get me a fair portion, that’s just stingy.

3. Served after people who ordered later.
I ordered first, yet multiple people who ordered after me received their food way earlier. The queue system felt completely disorganised, and there was no acknowledgment of the delay.

4. Odd and unprofessional interaction with another customer
I also witnessed the auntie being told off by another customer to stick her sticky note inside his takeaway container instead of outside. The whole interaction was awkward and showed a lack of basic service sense.

Back in the day, it was helmed by Uncle and his wife, whose Mee Hoon Kueh was nothing short of legendary in the neighbourhood — the kind of bowl that warms both the stomach and the soul. Restaurant Name: Trattoria Da Mimmo Restaurant And Pizzeria
Reviews:
Stepping into Trattoria Da Mimmo, one expects the warm, flour-dusted embrace of a traditional Italian kitchen. The atmosphere promises a rustic escape, yet the culinary journey that followed was a complex tapestry of artisanal brilliance marred by technical inconsistencies.

Burrata Pugliese - While the portion was undeniably generous—a gleaming orb of cheese that dominated the board—it was, alas, a masterclass in missed potential. The cheese lacked that essential, soul-warming milky sweetness, arriving somewhat muted and flavourless. It functioned more as a textural element than the star of the show.

Similarly, the Insalata Di Rucola offered an abundant mountain of greenery. However, the balance was skewed; the peppery arugula possessed an aggressive bitterness that overwhelmed the palate, lacking the necessary acidity or sweetness in the dressing to tame its wilder notes.

The Spaghetti Al Nero Di Seppia was a triumph. The jet-black strands were perfectly al dente, coated in a sauce that sang with the briny, umami-rich depths of the ocean. It was a dark, delicious embrace of coastal Italian tradition.

In stark contrast, the Fettuccine Al Salmone felt uninspired. The salmon lacked the vibrant, buttery flaking of a fresh catch, leaning towards a duller, "average" profile that failed to elevate the dish beyond standard trattoria fare.

However, the Strozapreti special (notably presented as beautifully cupped orecchiette in form) was an intriguing highlight. The texture was delightful, providing a nuanced chew that caught the sauce effectively—a truly enjoyable and creative diversion from the core menu.

Where Da Mimmo truly finds its rhythm is at the pizza station. Both the Pizza Hawaiian and the Pizza Prosciutto E Funghi were exceptionally well-crafted. The crusts bore the hallmark leopard-spotting of a well-stoked oven, providing a crisp foundation for the harmonious toppings. The Prosciutto E Funghi, in particular, displayed a wonderful earthiness, while the Hawaiian—often a point of contention—was handled with a refined balance of sweet and savoury.

The Cote De Boeuf was a heartbreaking encounter. Visually, the kitchen’s technique was evident; the doneness was a flawless, edge-to-edge ruby pink. Yet, the execution stumbled at the pass. The meat arrived at the table far too cold, which caused the fats to congeal and rendered the otherwise premium cut tough and laborious to chew. A dish that should have been a celebration of the Maillard reaction and succulent tenderness was instead dampened by poor temperature management.

Restaurant Name: Tsukada Nojo || Japanese Premium Hotpot || Collagen-Rich Chicken Stock || Thomson Plaza
Reviews:
Came here for their signature Bijin Nabe, and overall it was a satisfying and comforting hotpot experience.

The chicken collagen broth is the highlight — rich, silky and clean-tasting without being overly greasy. You can really tell it’s been simmered properly, and it becomes more flavourful as the ingredients cook. The white fish and prawns were fresh, sweet and cooked beautifully in the broth. The mushroom platter was generous and well-selected, adding natural umami depth to the soup.

I also liked the option to add beauty noodles at the end — light, springy, and a good way to soak up the remaining broth without feeling too heavy. Portions were adequate for sharing, and the meal felt balanced rather than indulgent.

The restaurant itself is bright and comfortable, though it can get quite busy during peak hours, which makes the space a bit noisy. Service was generally attentive, but timing between items could be smoother when the restaurant is full. Pricing is on the higher side for hotpot, but understandable given the quality of ingredients and concept.

Overall, a solid choice for Japanese-style collagen hotpot — comforting, well-executed, and ideal for a relaxed meal with friends or family. Would return, especially when craving a nourishing broth.

The portion of the beef stew with rice was way too small for $16. The rice was especially sad (almost the size of the spoon). Wouldn’t recommend the pho either due to similar complains. We all had to get a snack afterwards from ARC nearby.

A quiet, quaint cafe with a great selection of food. Had the pho and the Saturday special prawn noodle today. Both were delicious. Also got their Pandan lemongrass, which wasn’t too sweet. All in, we were very satisfied with the food. The location was a little out of the way, but the surprising thing was that their parking was free! Maybe it’s a Saturday/Sunday thing.

Found a hidden gem! Had a really satisfying meal here and would highly recommend this place.

We ordered the beef pho (beef balls + sliced beef) and it was excellent. The soup was very tasty and flavorful, and the beef slices were generous, fresh, and tender.

The turmeric fish with dill noodles is an interesting and unique dish worth trying. The fish was delicious, boneless, well-seasoned, and cooked perfectly.

The dry grilled chicken noodles were also very good. The noodles were smooth and the chicken was flavorful.

The mixed spring roll platter came with both fried and non-fried Vietnamese spring rolls. The ingredients were fresh and generous, and the fried ones were crispy without being greasy. Highly recommended.

We also tried the crème caramel, which was very good — not too sweet, just right, with a lovely fragrance from the burnt caramel.

The lemongrass pandan drinks tasted homemade, fragrant, and not overly sweet.

Service was friendly and great, and the food was served fast. Overall, the food here is excellent value for money. Portions are big, ingredients are fresh, and the seasoning is top class. Everything was well-balanced — not too sweet and not too salty. Will definitely be back.

Really wonderful find coming across this small hidden Vietnamese restaurant. All of the various dishes we tried including the pho and bun cha were very authentic and well done. Prices were very reasonable and the staff were so friendly! Highly recommended.
A bit pricey for a bistro even though the food is good.

Ordered two huge bowls of sharks fin amongst all things for two tables. The sharks fin come overly starched and salty, with little sharks fin found within. Some of my guests did not consume their sharks fin. Being a shark fin lover, I had half left in my bowl as it was really too starchy and salty. No one got a second serving despite 1/3 left in the huge bowl after serving 9 pax. I gave a bowl of sharks fin for the staff to try, but was told that the sharks fin was indeed too starchy but not overly salty. The restaurant did not agreed with my request to cancel that order, but compensated with free desserts (longan) instead. I do think that nothing is perfect and everyone makes mistake. It will be great if they accept the issue and make proper amends. However, if they cannot recognize that a dish was indeed badly done, I think there is no further need to revisit.

Thumbs up for the wonderful service and keep up the good vibes!

As a dog owner who lives nearby, i'm a regular here and always looking to try their seasonal specials. Food is great and prices are reasonable. Their mee siam is v popular, and I also like their tomato soup, clams, aglio, chicken bowl, cakes and cinnamon bread. Their fizzy drinks are perfect for a lazy afternoon too.
Their staff are very sweet and attentive to dog owners. I rmb vividly that I was there alone with my dog on a public holiday, and not only were the staff (yes all of them) in good spirits, one of them took it upon himself to stand at my table and keep an eye on my dog while i went inside to settle the bill. (They can take the card reader to the table too, but I was in a hurry that day and thought to do a quick run to the till).
W39 has been around for years and I truly hope that there will be more to come. The food and the people here are deserving of our support.

Very nice people and if you have pets the sitting area is outside, with ceiling fans and despite us going at the  hot midday timing, it was nice with the fans,  and the awning definitely shields so  we could  enjoy the delicious food comfortably. There are water bowls and tap conveniently located and there’s a small but nice park just to the right of this place. The doggy received a free treat too.

The waiter bothered to swop a chair with a backing when he noticed my 90 year old mom.

I saw cars stopping by to do takeaways and people popping in to  buy bread too.
Regular haunt. Food is good but most of all staff are amazing.
Great vibes in a neighborhood that is thinning out in terms of crowd and consumption

I had a disappointing experience here due to the poor service and lack of transparency.

Despite ordering 1 mains, 1 side and drinks for 2, our server repeatedly pressured us to order more drinks, making us feel like we were not "justifying" our table. To top it off, she dropped the bill at our table without us asking and basically told us to leave because others were waiting. Incredibly rude and unprofessional.

Being hovered over and then pushed out the door is not hospitality. If there are house policies regarding spending or time, they should be clearly communicated upfront, not used to harass guests.

I recommend that you save your money and go somewhere that actually wants your business.

The vibe is back in Holland V! Nice new fresh look! The live band adds so much to this institution! Congratulations to Team Wala Wala on such a wonderful revamp! Kudos.

One of the table has 3 ladies on it but its joint by 3 tables. He told me that they reserved for 14 pax. However from 7 to 9, only the 3 were there. That particular staff is rude and did not keep his promise to release the table to us. It is very disappointing.

PLEASE close your shop and let other business come. What a stupid menu, we MUST buy cold drinks with ice cream and price difference almost $2 by itself. So lame and so dumb, no card payments. It was my first time visiting. There were seats available around 3 - 4 PM. I ordered milk tea, condensed milk Bun and crispy noodles with sliced beef and eggs. Out of these three items, I would say the noodles were worth the try. Maybe switching out with other noodles would taste better. For ordering and payment, you will have to mark it on the menu and head to the cashier to pay. There is no complimentary water and tissue provided.

2nd Visit - Beef Brisket Noodle, Polo Bun and Ice Lemon Tea. I liked the Ice Lemon Tea the most. As I was dining alone, midway into my noodles, the staff asked if I wanted chilli. I was surprised and appreciative of the gesture.

After the Covid19 hiatus, finally got the chance to dine here. The fried rice is really wonderful wif much wok hei....and so is the fried hor fun! (The bright yellowish egg yolk was so presentable!)
Worth reporting here wif no regrets after spending $49.80!

Enjoyed my experience here. Food has no gst, service charge. Everything is net. Do note they dont take credit card payment. Generous portions, decent taste, not too overly salty nor bland. My go to Korean restaurant in SG to satisfy my Korean cuisine cravings, something that is hearty and value for money to me.

Have been coming back here many times and it never disappoints as the consistency is always there. I like that they have a fixed menu everyday and you just have to show up and have it served to you, without thinking much about what to eat.

My favourite dishes would be the Bulgogi (generous amount of meat) & seasoned fried chicken! Honourable mention goes to the homemade waffle for dessert 😋  Although it’s a very small piece, i really like the texture of it because it is the chewy kind, similar to mochi, served warm.

The friendly male boss is also very dedicated to his job & can give this place a try if you’re around the area! Can use CDC vouchers too ~

Wang Family Kitchen - this Korean family-run restaurant has been in operation for quite a number of years at Hillview Community Club, and its enduring presence thereat is testament to its no-fuss, no-nonsense, comfortingly delicious Korean meal sets served daily as a "Day Plate" and at a reasonable price. My wife and I have dined here on a number of occasions and we have always been satisfied with the place. As we sort of live "just across the road" in the Dairy Farm area, choosing this place for a Korean meal is a no-brainer. Service here is nice enough, and the dining ambience is comfortable. I recommend that you try this place for its home-cooked style Korean food, if you are in the Hillview area.

Home cooked taste and mostly only 1 set meal choice. Variety is limited and almost daily same dishes are served. Wish they would have 2 set choices with fish /seafood variety too. This store tends to serve chicken & pork as mains in 1 set meal. I rather have 1 main meat choice & more side dish varieties. Their samygetang [ginseng chicken] is popular too. Price is reasonable.

Highly recommend Uncle’s chicken feet noodles — a must order!
The chicken feet are braised until soft and full of collagen, rich and flavorful, and they go perfectly with the noodles. Definitely something you shouldn’t miss if it’s your first time here.

I give credit where credit is due. Honestly, this is one coffeeshop where mostly residents staying around here will visit and eat as the ever popular 505 Jurong west market & food centre is just a walking distance. I love this Bak Chor Mee and potion is good too. Keeps me full and satisfied with a happy smile. Do order the number 2. Uncle may look fierce or arrogant but he is not. He says thank you too. If you are around here, give this a try. If you look at the operating timing, sells till afternoon so it will be a disappointment if you are expecting to open late evening or night. If i come here. It will usually be in the morning so it’s alright.
The uncle owner attitude is worse act like he don't worry no customers come.after I buy from this stall one time I don't feel go eat again

My visit to Whampoa Keng Fish Head Steamboat was a standout dining experience that truly showcased the depth and comfort of traditional Singaporean cuisine. Known for its signature charcoal-cooked steamboat, the restaurant delivered both flavour and authenticity from the moment the dish arrived.

The highlight was, without a doubt, the fish head steamboat. Served bubbling in a claypot over charcoal, the broth was rich, slightly milky, and deeply infused with the sweetness of fresh seafood. The fish head itself was tender and flaky, absorbing the soup beautifully. Accompanied by napa cabbage, tofu, yam, and other ingredients, the dish felt hearty and well-balanced.

What made the experience even more enjoyable was the nostalgic cooking method. The use of charcoal added a subtle smokiness that elevated the overall flavour, setting it apart from more modern steamboat styles. It also created a warm, communal dining atmosphere.

Service was efficient and no-nonsense, typical of many well-loved local establishments. Despite the busy environment, dishes arrived promptly and staff were attentive when needed.

Overall, Whampoa Keng Fish Head Steamboat offered an authentic and satisfying meal. It’s a must-visit for anyone seeking a traditional, flavour-rich dining experience in Singapore. Highly recommended!!!

I’m extremely disappointed with my repeated experiences at Xin Yuan Ji at Lentor Modern. This is not a one-time issue, it has happened three times, and enough is enough.
Residents at Lentor Modern are supposed to receive a 10% discount. We even confirmed this with the staff beforehand, and she acknowledged that the discount applies. However, when it came to payment, she keyed in the full amount and asked us to pay immediately. It is our negligence that we didn’t double-check on the spot as it felt stressful to hold up the person and trusted that the discount had already been applied.
A major red flag was that she didn’t even offer a receipt. It was only after I confronted her that she printed it, which then revealed that the discount had not been applied at all. Her explanation? She “forgot” to key it in. But this exact same situation has happened three separate times, which makes it very hard to believe it’s accidental.
When we requested a refund for the missed discount, we were told it couldn’t be done because it was already keyed into the system. Instead, the staff tried to compensate by offering to “add more ingredients.” This is not an acceptable solution. The added items were either not what we wanted (e.g., tofu), or in previous cases, there was no noticeable difference at all especially for takeaway orders where they claimed to add more vegetables.
This pattern of behaviour feels dishonest and misleading. Customers should not have to repeatedly check whether they are being charged correctly, especially after confirming a promotion with staff.
Overall, this experience has been extremely frustrating. I hope the management takes this seriously, as it reflects poorly on the integrity of the business.

(Update: This stall will permanently close by the end of June 2026 as there are not enough customers to keep the business going due to low footfall at the coffeeshop.
(The much-raved ‘Oh My Don’ Japanese stall has already shut due to this)
So best enjoy the food before this stall shuts permanently!)

This stall is run by a very friendly middle-age couple previously from China.
Their ban mian/u mian noodle which the husband painstakingly kneads by hand every morning (no machine is used) is consistently very good.
What sets this stall apart from other ban mian stalls is that they have fried u mian and fried bee hoon which is very Heng Hwa style on their menu.
What’s more, they are flexible to tweet the ingredients depending on customer’s dietary restrictions.
For instance, as I am a pescatarian, the ingredients for my order of fried u mian or fried bee hoon can be changed to fish slices instead of the usual la la, etc  .
The owner is even very readily willing to fry ban mian when requested…
It is something customers never get to taste anywhere else in Singapore.
The stall’s dumplings are big and delicious too - value for money.
Plus, they give fresh green vegetables instead of the usual cabbage and the fish they use is fresh batang instead of the cheap tilapia…
Highly recommended…

Reviews:
Went to YAYOI @ 100AM for a weekday lunch during the CNY period. The restaurant was relatively quiet around noon, which made it a comfortable spot for a group lunch (we had 6 pax).

We ordered several teishoku sets - Amazu Chicken Steak, Hakata Mizutaki, Namban & Ebi Fry, Tori Katsu Toji, and Sukiyaki, along with their Salmon Yu Sheng for the festive season (it was repeatedly recommended by their staff).

The portions of their mains were generous, but my Amazu Chicken Steak had too much sauce, which overpowered the entire dish. A few of my colleagues felt the same about their dishes - meat was nicely cooked, but way too saucy overall.

That said, the value of their lunch meals is pretty good. Each teishoku set comes with rice, miso soup, and access to the free refill counter. The salad bar was a nice touch as it had cherry tomatoes, corn, pickled ginger and other small sides that you can help yourself to. The unlimited rice and miso soup definitely made it more satisfying, especially for bigger eaters. The hojicha (both hot and iced) was also included in the lunch set :)

The highlight for us was actually the Salmon Yu Sheng. The ingredients were fresh, the salmon sashimi slices were thick, and the overall mix was well-balanced. Really yummy!

Overall, mains were slightly underwhelming due to the saltiness, but the free refills and seasonal offerings helped balance out the experience. A decent option for a casual weekday lunch, especially if you value set meals with unlimited sides :)

We ordered the Teochew Braised Set with a bowl of Kway 潮州卤味套餐, along with an extra serving of Braised Beancurd Skin 卤香焖腐竹.

The kway was soaked in a lightly herbal, comforting soup, paired with a richer and thicker lor chap. Ingredients like the braised duck meat, fish cake, tau pok and more came together really well with the silky kway. Every mouthful felt hearty and satisfying.

My SO especially loved the warmth of the soup, perfect for a cozy dinner. The braised beancurd skin was flavourful too, soft yet structured, and absorbed the braise nicely.

A simple, comforting Teochew-style meal that hits the spot. 🍜✨
