PREVIOUS REVIEW (4 Stars):
I decided to try Zi Jia Yong Tau Foo at Timbre+ Hillview, and my experience was a mix of highs and lows. The quality of the yong tau foo itself is fantastic and definitely a highlight.

Let's start with the best part: the ingredients. Each piece of yong tau foo I selected was fresh, flavourful, and expertly cooked. The fried items had a wonderful savoury taste, and the stuffed pieces were delicious. In terms of the core product, the quality is easily comparable to other top-tier YTF stalls I've enjoyed.

Unfortunately, there was a mix-up with my order which affected the final dish. I had ordered the dry version with kway teow, but I was initially served the soup version with the YTF pieces on the side. To their credit, they were quick to rectify it. However, the method of correction—simply pouring the soup away from the noodles and then combining everything into a dry bowl—seemed to have an unfortunate side effect.

I'm not sure if this was the direct cause, but the kway teow ended up being overcooked, soft, and mushy, lacking that smooth, springy texture that makes the dish enjoyable.

Despite the disappointing noodles, the meal was saved by the sheer quality of the yong tau foo pieces. For that reason, I'm giving it a solid 4 stars. I would definitely be willing to return, as the ingredients are clearly top-notch. Next time, I'll be sure to double-check my order and perhaps try a different noodle option.

We ordered their pu er tea by the pot, barley, prawn dumplings, steamed siew mai 烧卖, chicken claws 凤爪 and pork ribs with yam. It was ok at best, but since the grandparents like it, we always come back here for brunch as a family. The lady boss is not very cordial with her staff, and tends to scold them in front of the customers. I can see that the usual crowd has diminished significantly over the years, as food and service has dipped.
It was good. My parents likes it👍🏻

Decided to drop by this restaurant after passing by many times.

May be out of way but an ideal place for a good meal away from urban crowds.

Went there to celebrate my dad’s birthday. Location wide damm ulu so we drove there. Food wise it’s 东北 food so some may not like, my parents allright with such Chinese food.

We loved the 回锅肉 and the 番茄蛋 the most they were delicious! The vegetables also tasty. Be warned China cooking uses a lot of oil hence the dishes are oily and salty. There was a 25% discount of minimum $100 spent on food ONLY (does not include drinks and alcohol) so we whack 6 dishes haha. It’s akin to one free dish. Hence we overate and I felt super bloated from the oil 🙊 There was also a mini game where I rolled a can on the table and see where it lands to enjoy certain perks for the month, but I rolled the can off the table hence no second chances :( Will be back someday!
工业区内，离居民区远，个人感觉新加坡最好的中国风味羊肉串，菜价偏高，味道偏好。

We arrived at around 7 PM on July 29th for a family dinner. While the food was decent, the service was exceptionally slow. We found ourselves waiting until almost 8:30 to 9 PM, and all our dishes hadn't been served by then. In the end, we had to cancel some dishes because it was getting very late.

As we were preparing to leave, we noticed something quite disturbing. When pouring water from the teapot, we discovered numerous insects inside. It appeared that the teapot hadn't been cleaned properly, and this was evident from its dirty condition when we opened it. Shockingly, we had been drinking water from this contaminated teapot, which was highly unpleasant.

After informing the staff about the issue, their response was not very apologetic. However, they did offer a 20% discount on the bill. Overall, this was my second visit to the establishment, and regrettably, it will also be my last.
I didn't know they got break time.. arrive and they told me they are eating. But nothing on the Google state they close for noon

the 1pax army stew’s portion was decent - a packet of seaweed, a bowl of rice and half packet of ramyeon. the pork katsu was thin, crispy and complimented well with the sweet bbq sauce. overall a decent meal spent $34+ for two mains.

My single pancake was eventually served at 12:59pm - a 40-minute wait for a simple item. Such a prolonged delay, coupled with the billing discrepancy, reflects poorly on the stall’s operational standards and service integrity. This experience has significantly undermined my confidence in this stall.
Excellent service, the food is yummy n price reasonable. Will definitely come back again. 😋

My first sushi takeaway was at gogo Causeway Point. It was so fresh, good, and reasonably priced, and it has since been my go-to place whenever I crave sushi. It was a great grab-and-go meal as the sushi was well packed. Today, I was at Yew Tee and chanced upon the shop; without hesitation, I went in to purchase Sushi Don. It's so good.
Sushiro gogo offers takeaway only, making it quick and convenient. The sushi was well packed and reasonably priced. A good choice for a simple grab-and-go meal.

I come here regularly almost every week for the past year to get the sashimi and mentaiko sushi. I usually call before coming down after 9pm to check if they are still available. For the past week, I’ve tried calling almost everyday after 9pm, but no one ever answers the phone😠 What’s the point of having the phone number then…

Edit: The situation has improved slightly since I posted my review though sometimes still no one picks up depending on the staff present. Staff Wei Ye is friendly and always answers the call.

One of the best xiao long bao I have had, better than the likes of din tai feng. The tomato lala soup is tasty and vermicili is cooked to perfection. Quite a long time to wait for the XLBs to be steamed tho.
5 chicken and 5 pork satay. Not bad, abit sweet.
Had Ban Mian and Red Wine Chicken Mee Sua for lunch. Nicely served with soft boiled egg. Perfect comfort food. Owner Mr Li was very friendly too.
It is hard to find a stall that makes such nostalgic pancakes after the closing of the Lavender hawker centre. Get your quick fix here.
Awesome old school pancakes eat while it’s hot
Good

Donkey and I visited 江湖冒菜 at Junction 10 with our cycling friends. When we arrived, the restaurant felt warm. Staff explained the air conditioning was centrally controlled by the mall and could not be adjusted, so we asked for a fan to be directed towards our table, which was done promptly.

After ordering, we waited about 30 minutes for our food. When we asked about the delay, staff told us they had been taking their dinner break, which we felt was unprofessional.

We ordered a variety of dishes, including Special Marinated Beef, Beef Tendon, Lamb Kebab, Grilled Corn, Grilled Potato Slices, Salted Egg Pumpkin, Sichuan Spicy Chicken, Grilled Bun, along with beers and bottled drinks. The total bill came to $92.45 including GST.

Drinks are self service and beer is cheap, but the food did not match the standard we experienced at other branches. The stew was much spicier than expected, leaving leftovers as most of our friends could not handle the spice. Other dishes were acceptable but inconsistent compared to what we had elsewhere.

Food 3/5
Service 2/5
Atmosphere 2/5
Overall 2/5

Very nice. Must return to try their other items especially the spicy wantan noodle.
Love the fried rice & spicy wantons. Tasty food at a affordable price! Conveniently located at Clementi. Worth the visit!
Yummy fried rice and succulent pork chop only $6.50 at this newly opened stall at Clementi West. Can try their Mala noodle too. Their chicken wings are huge and flavourful.
Really enjoyed this fried rice. Not too heavy and salty. Can finish it. Plus the toppings are really meaty. I love the wontons too.
Love their fried rice, pork chop and chicken cutlet. It’s really nice and yummy! The 红油抄手 is also delicious! Had a good lunch with my friend! Do give it a try :)

Today, on my way to work, I made a quick stop at the canteen in Pioneer Sector 2. It had been a while since I visited, and there were some new stalls to check out. I decided to give Roasted Delight a try, and I'm so glad I did!

Roasted Delight is a simple stall run by a friendly Chinese national.  I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious their roasted meat and char siew were.  I ordered a mix of both, and they really loaded up the portions.  It was incredibly generous for just $5!

The meat was tender and flavorful, and the char siew had a lovely glaze.  It was a perfect combination of savory and sweet.  The owner was also very friendly and welcoming, making my morning routine even more enjoyable.

It was a great way to start my day, and I'm definitely going to make a point of stopping by again sometime.  I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and affordable breakfast option in the area.

The ambiance is comfortable and elegant, suitable for family meals or casual gatherings. Overall, a solid dim sum spot that I would come back to.

A very welcome addition to Greenwood, which had previously been a row of Western restaurants. The food is excellent and authentically Teochew, and the service is excellent, in particular Carmen and Hui Xian were very charming and friendly!
We enjoyed our meal here. The chai poh kway teow is excellent! We also enjoyed the candied walnut and the preserved mango slices. We were served by Carmen and Leslie, with very good service.

Came here for lunch and honestly, the food was pretty normal. Nothing particularly memorable, but not terrible either.
The ban mian soup was slightly flavourful, but it didn’t leave much of an impact. It’s decent enough for a simple lunch, just not something I would specifically crave for.
The fish soup tasted good when it was hot. However, once it turned warm, the flavour seemed to disappear. There was also quite a lot of bitter gourd in it, which made the soup a bit too bitter for my liking.
The steamed fish was unfortunately not that good as it had a slight muddy taste. That was a bit disappointing.
One thing I did enjoy was the chilli sauce for dipping the fish. One of the versions was sour and spicy, which I really liked. It added some excitement to the meal.
Overall, I think it’s still a decent place for a simple meal, just don’t expect anything mind blowing.

JH Fishball Noodles is a beloved hawker stall in Singapore’s Teban Gardens Wet Market & Food Centre, known for serving classic, no-frills fishball noodles at wallet-friendly prices. Operating since the 1980s, it has become a go-to breakfast spot for locals seeking traditional comfort food.

I had the Fishball Noodles (dry) for $2.50 — a small portion as expected at that price, but just right for breakfast. The noodles were springy, the fishballs fresh and bouncy, and the seasoning was well balanced. Just note that it closes by 2pm, so come early. I’d rate it a 4 out of 5 — simple, satisfying, and a dependable start to the day.

The black fried carrot cake was quite ordinary, soft in some parts, a bit soggy in others, and overall not to my liking. The seasoning didn’t stand out, though the portion was decent. If you like DRY CHUNKY Carrot Cake, that is not too sweet and slimy, you will be very very please to dry this. If you like the wet slimy smashed up carrot cake, go somewhere else; you will be disappointed. So you can stop reading now.
Believe it or not, it is so difficult to find carrot cake that are DRY AND CHUNKY, so that you actually taste the "Carrot Cake" itself. They actually do have a smell and taste by itself, without the egg, without the sauce. However when it is smashed up ant meshed with the egg, sauce, and whatever not, you have a pancake of some sort.
Back in the day when we eat carrot cake, they are big chunks, fried in a huge flat round pan. And the carrot cake are seared to perfection, then the sweet sauce and chili are put on top of it. And then the last is the egg (pay 10 cents more). This is served in large green leave, clipped together with toothpick. Man, I wish I could have that today.... So this stall come close to it (not exactly at all), and it's satisfying!
You have the option to have "Ebony and Ivory", amazingly some people like it white :P (incomprehensible). But to each his/her own.
Their biggest strength they have a good amount of Chye Poh and Garlic, and the egg is NOT too overwhelming. And most of all the sweetness is very tamed and with a good touch of saltiness.
Go before 10am, or else be prepared to queue. I'm dead serious.
I'm going next week, hopefully every week!!

I've now visited Danlao twice, and it's clear that the choice of topping makes all the difference. This is a solid spot for a comforting scrambled egg rice bowl, especially if you know what to order.

On both my visits, the two constants were the egg and the rice. As the name suggests, their scrambled egg good—cooked just right, soft and creamy, blanketing the rice underneath. While it's good and competently made, I wouldn't call it spectacular. The rice was also consistently well-cooked, with distinct grains (粒粒分明) and not mushy at all.

My first visit was a bit of a letdown. I had the Cheesy Char Siew bowl. The char siew was unfortunately on the dry side, and the "cheesy" element was simply a slice of processed cheese laid on top that hadn't fully melted. It felt like an afterthought and didn't add much to the dish.

However, my second visit was a significant improvement and the reason for the 4-star rating. I ordered the Classic Luncheon Meat and added on a Chicken Cutlet. The chicken cutlet was the undeniable highlight of the meal—perfectly crispy, juicy, and flavourful. It provided a fantastic textural contrast to the soft eggs and rice. The luncheon meat was standard fare, good but not memorable.

In conclusion, Danlao offers a satisfying meal, but the experience can be hit-or-miss depending on your protein choice. Based on my visits, I'd highly recommend skipping the char siew and going straight for the fried items, especially the excellent chicken cutlet.
